Postdoctoral position in functional ancient microbial ecogenomics within the Ancient Environmental Genomics Initiative for Sustainability (AEGIS)

Section for GeoGenetics

Globe Institute

Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences

University of Copenhagen

The Ancient Environmental Genomics Initiative for Sustainability (AEGIS) invites applications for three two-year postdoctoral positions in functional ancient microbial ecology, starting 1 November 2026, or as soon as possible thereafter. We seek one researcher in each of three areas: computational ancient metabolomics and natural products, carbohydrate-active enzymes and carbohydrate metabolism, and protein language models for ancient metagenomics.

Our research

AEGIS is a pioneering research centre headed by Prof. Eske Willerslev that brings together a highly interdisciplinary and international team of world-leading research groups with a shared vision of developing more robust, sustainable, and biodiverse crops and agricultural practices to mitigate the effects of climate change on global food production: https://novonordiskfonden.dk/en/news/climate-resilient-crops-novo-nordisk-foundation-and-the-wellcome-trust-award-a-grant-of-up-to-dkk-585-million-to-the-ancient-environmental-genomics-initiative-for-sustainability/

AEGIS combines ancient environmental DNA, genomics, metagenomics, informatics and biostatistics, evolutionary biology, ecology, geology, archaeology, plant engineering, and agricultural crop research. We will collect and work on geological sediments, bones, fossils, and material from contemporary species from more than 200 locations worldwide to generate and analyse vast amounts of ancient and contemporary environmental DNA and other ancient and modern biomolecular data, along with associated contextual data.

The advertised positions are within the Microbial EcoGenomics Group at the Center for Ancient Environmental Genomics. The group leverages ancient DNA (aDNA) to reconstruct past microbial ecosystems, understand long-term biodiversity dynamics, and innovate computational methods for analysing ancient microbial data.

We value diversity and inclusivity in our research community. We actively encourage applications from individuals of all backgrounds, identities, and experiences who share our commitment to addressing global environmental challenges through innovative research.

Your job

As a postdoctoral researcher, you will analyse large-scale ancient environmental DNA (aeDNA) datasets generated through high-throughput sequencing technologies. You will investigate how the functional potential of microbial communities has changed across time and space. The aim is to understand which microorganisms were present in past ecosystems, what functions they could perform, and how these functions changed through time. The three positions will address this by studying carbohydrate-active enzymes, biosynthetic gene clusters and natural products, and developing protein language models for functional annotation of ancient metagenomes.

Together, these areas will help us investigate how past microbial communities used organic matter and produced compounds involved in interactions among microorganisms, plants and their environments. Work on ancient metabolomics and natural products will focus on computational analysis of biosynthetic genes and pathways, with analysis of metabolomics datasets where available. Work on carbohydrate metabolism will examine CAZymes and associated pathways in ancient and modern metagenomes. Protein language models will be used to predict the functions of proteins recovered from ancient DNA, including incomplete and poorly characterised sequences, and support these analyses.

Your responsibilities will include developing computational and statistical methods to study microbial functions in ancient metagenomic data. You will work with the other postdoctoral researchers and colleagues across AEGIS to evaluate functional predictions and interpret them in an ecological and evolutionary context.

Profile

We are looking for three scientists with experience in ancient metagenomics and expertise relevant to one of the three research areas. Applicants are not expected to have expertise in all three areas.

Essential Experience And Skills

You have a PhD in bioinformatics, genomics, community ecology, computational biology, computational metabolomics or a related field.
You have experience analysing large-scale ancient metagenomic datasets.
You have experience investigating microbial genes, metabolic pathways, functional traits or community-level processes in an ecological or evolutionary context.
You have experience with ancient or degraded DNA analysis, including authentication and the analysis of low-abundance and fragmented sequence data.
For the protein language model position, you have experience implementing and evaluating machine learning models for protein sequences.
Strong analytical skills and an interest in interdisciplinary research.
Proficient communication skills and ability to work in teams
Excellent English skills, written and spoken

Desirable Experience And Skills

Experience with computational metabolomics, natural product bioinformatics or biosynthetic gene cluster analysis; CAZyme annotation or microbial carbohydrate metabolism; or protein language models and protein function prediction, depending on the position applied for.
Computational skills, including proficiency in R, Python, or other relevant programming languages.
Experience working with high-performance computing (HPC) environments.
Strong scientific track record with publications in peer-reviewed international journals as first author in the field of microbial community and/or bioinformatics, genomics, ecological modelling, ancient DNA or similar.
Experience with startups, entrepreneurship, or innovation, particularly translating academic research and scientific findings into commercially relevant applications, or startup ventures

Place of employment

The place of employment is at the Globe Institute, Section for GeoGenetics (Øster Voldgade 5-7, 1350, Copenhagen), Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen.

About Globe Institute

The Globe Institute is part of the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences at the University of Copenhagen. The Institute’s main purpose is to address basic scientific questions through interdisciplinary approaches. The institute operates at the intersection of natural and medical sciences and the humanities. Information on the institute can be found at: https://www.globe.ku.dk/.

Globe Institute is committed to creating an inclusive and diverse environment where employees and students can belong and thrive. See the website for more information. All qualified applicants will receive full consideration. Candidates who, through their research, teaching, and/or service, contribute to diversity and competencies of our Institute are encouraged to apply. The University of Copenhagen strives to offer a family-friendly and flexible working environment with a sustainable balance between work and private life, including parental leave schemes (up to 47 weeks for both parents) and up to six weeks of paid holidays per year. Researchers who have not been tax liable in Denmark for the last 10 years can apply for a special (reduced) tax scheme. The university offers a variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families.

Terms of employment

The average weekly working hours are 37 hours per week.

The position is a fixed-term position limited to a period of 2 years. The starting date is on 1 November 2026, or as soon as possible thereafter.

The position is covered by the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff.

Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State.

There will be an opportunity to negotiate supplements based on qualifications. You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

Questions

: antonio.fernandez-guerra@sund.ku.dk

Postdoc in Embryo Epigenetics

We are looking for a highly motivated and dynamic researcher for a 3-year postdoctoral position, with the possibility of extension, to commence January 2027 or after agreement.

The position will be based in the Stewart-Morgan group at the Department for Cellular and Molecular Medicine (ICMM) within the University of Copenhagen. Information on the group can be found at: https://icmm.ku.dk/english/research-groups/stewart-morgan-group/

Our research

The focus of the Stewart-Morgan group is epigenetic dynamics and mammalian development. We use both in vivo and in vitro systems to study the role of the epigenome in development. We strive for an open, collaborative and collegial work environment that provides ample mentorship and training opportunities to further each members’ individual career goals.

Your job

Your tasks will include designing experimental strategies, generation and analysis of complex datasets, and writing of scientific manuscripts. Additional tasks could include contributing to grant applications, research-based supervision of MSc and PhD students, teaching undergraduate courses, and outreach communication activities.

Profile

We are looking for a highly motivated and enthusiastic scientist with the following competencies and experience:

Essential Experience And Skills

You have a PhD in life sciences or a similar field
You have experience in mouse genetics

Proficient communication skills and ability to work in teams

Experience in mouse embryology

ICMM aims to produce research with high international impact focusing on the functional cell, its genetic components, and molecular cellular mechanisms in a medical context. Our research facilities include modern laboratories, dedicated facilities for flow cytometry, imaging, next-generation sequencing including single-cell genomics, and state-of-the-art embryology facilities for mouse and human research.

jobs.title: PhD scholarship in Foundation Models for Clinical Bioinformatics and Cancer Prevention - DTU Health Tech
jobs.location: Kongens Lyngby, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
jobs.description:
Job Description

Are you interested in becoming a bioinformatics researcher working to improve the treatment and prognoses of colorectal cancer patients?

Then this is the position for you. You will join the ongoing efforts of researchers at the Department of Health Technology at the Technical University of Denmark and the Center for Surgical Science (CSS) at the University Hospital Zealand in Køge. The overall aim of this project is to integrate phenotypic data from national population-wide registries with multi omics data generated to characterize colorectal cancer samples and ultimately predict postoperative recurrence of the disease.

Responsibilities And Qualifications

You will work at the interface of artificial intelligence, bioinformatics, and clinical research. The project aims to develop novel computational models that integrate nationwide longitudinal health data with microbiome and genomic data to better understand adenoma-to-carcinoma progression and support clinically relevant decision-making. The candidate will contribute to the development of foundation models for sequence data and patient trajectories, representation learning approaches for microbial genomes and microbiomes, and predictive models linking molecular and clinical data to cancer risk stratification.

The work will be carried out in close collaboration with computational researchers at DTU and clinical experts at the Center for Surgical Science. The project offers a unique opportunity to work with nationwide Danish health registries, large-scale microbiome datasets, and state-of-the-art machine learning methods.

You are expected to:

Develop and apply machine learning and foundation-model approaches for large-scale longitudinal health data and large-scale genomic data.
Integrate clinical, microbiome, and genomic data to uncover factors associated with adenoma progression and colorectal cancer development.
Develop computational representations of patient trajectories and microbial communities using modern AI and bioinformatics methodologies.

The following qualifications are required:

A master's degree in bioinformatics, computer science, computational biology, data science, biomedical engineering, statistics, or a related quantitative field.
Experience with statistical analysis and machine learning.
Experience handling and analyzing large-scale biological or health-related datasets.

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment

The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education .

We offer

DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms

The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. The allowance will be agreed upon with the relevant union. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures .

The period of employment is 3 years. The starting date is 1 December 2026 or after mutual agreement.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here .

Further information

Further information may be obtained from Ole Lund, olund@dtu.dk .

You can read more about DTU Health at www.healthtech.dtu.dk/english and www.healthtech.dtu.dk/english/research/research-sections/section-bioinformatics .

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark . Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “ PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar ” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU.

Application procedure

Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 18 September 2026 (23:59 Danish time)
. Applications must be submitted as one PDF file
containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file
. The file must include:

A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
Curriculum vitae
Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale

You may apply prior to ob­tai­ning your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it.

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829

DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

jobs.title: Senior Data Scientist - System Optimization
jobs.location: Copenhagen, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
jobs.description:
The Impact You'll Make

Are you an experienced data scientist who wants to model how real energy networks physically behave — and then optimize across them?

Join Danfoss Digital Solutions, Utility, and help unlock the flexibility of district energy in the green transition.

The Vision We Are Building Towards

District heating and cooling utilities are facing their most demanding transition yet — changing production sources, electrified heat, volatile energy markets and a hard decarbonization mandate — operated, for the most part, with tools that optimize one asset or one hour at a time.

Our ambition is system-level optimization across production, network and demand, so that a utility can bring the best possible energy-economic value while honoring its decarbonization commitments.

What You’ll Be Doing

We are looking for a Senior Data Scientist to deepen the modelling and optimization core of our Utility team. You will apply mathematical modeling, programming skills and optimization theory to ensure our products deliver maximal value to our customers.

Some Of The Key Activities Will Include

Develop and extend our thermo-hydraulic simulation tools for district energy networks by applying physical modelling principles — flow, pressure and temperature dynamics across the network — augmented with machine learning and data driven methods.
Calibrate and validate the physical models against live network measurements, closing the loop between simulation, real operating data, and the hydraulic behavior of the networks we run.
Advance our production optimization solutions, where Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) and related techniques plan heat production and storage across grid-scale utilities.
Connect the layers into system-level optimization — production, network and demand treated as one problem, from heat producers through to consumers, including demand-side response.
Build and develop the data pipelines your models depend on, together with our data engineering platform team.
Own the problem and communicate with our customers – deeply understand the problem to solve, possible solution discovery, prototyping and validation. You can communicate technical solutions to non-technical collaboration partners.

The Team

Your main development team is based in Denmark, working with colleagues across several European locations. Beyond your daily team, you join a data science community in Denmark of experienced data scientists working on problems next to yours — production optimization, thermo-hydraulic network simulation, temperature optimization and forecasting. You will have people to think out loud with, review your models and challenge your assumptions, and you will do the same for them.

What We're Looking For

You are an experienced data scientist who knows how to solve complex problems by applying data modelling. You have experience working in a large development team in a modern software development environment. You own the problem and solution and at the same time collaborate with the team to make it happen.

On top of that, you should be able to check off as many of the following as possible:

Hold a Master’s degree or higher in a relevant quantitative field (mathematics, machine learning, statistics, physics, engineering, etc.)
PhD degree is a benefit, but not a strict requirement
Several years of experience applying data modelling to complex physical or industrial systems
Excellent command of Python as this is used as our main programming tool
Solid knowledge of district energy and thermo-hydraulic simulation — experience with physical modelling of flow, pressure and temperature in fluid networks is central to this role
Familiarity with numerical methods for simulating dynamic physical systems, and calibrating such models with measurement data
Experience in solving complex optimization problems, for example with Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP), is an advantage
Experience with C# and C++ is appreciated, as these are used for some of our legacy solutions
Fluent in English
Willing to apply and learn about advanced methodology in the district energy field
Interested in blending physical models of heating and cooling systems with data-driven methods

Location

This position is based in our office in Copenhagen or Kolding, Denmark — Copenhagen preferred. We work closely as a team on site, and we are looking for someone who will be based in one of these two locations.

What You'll Get From Us

At Danfoss, we are engineering solutions that allow the world to use resources in smarter ways — driving the sustainable transformation of tomorrow.

Purpose-driven work. District energy is one of the most effective levers for decarbonising heat. The models you build shape how much fuel is burned, how much CO₂ is emitted, and how much value a utility can capture from flexible operation.

Depth, and the mandate to go deeper. Physics-based modelling of real networks is where our expertise sits and where we intend to stay ahead. This is not a feature factory — the hard modelling problem is the product.

Growth. We value continuous development and encourage it through courses, rotations and career tracks.

We believe that innovation and great results are driven by the right mix of people with diverse backgrounds, personalities, skills, and perspectives, reflecting the world in which we do business.

Ready to Make a Difference?

If this role excites you, we’d love to hear from you! Apply now to start the conversation and learn more about where your career can go with us.

Our Commitment to Transparency

Salary ranges listed reflect only primary location and currency. For local salary ranges and specific benefits in your preferred hiring location, please ask your Talent Acquisition representative for more information.

The actual salary offer will carefully consider a wide range of factors, including your skills, qualifications, experience, and location. Any benefits listed do not promise or guarantee any particular benefit or specific action. They may depend on country or contract specifics and are subject to change at any time without prior notice.

Want to know more? Please visit our FAQ Page.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or other protected category.

jobs.title: Data Scientist - Energy Forecasting
jobs.location: Copenhagen, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
jobs.description:
The Impact You'll Make

Are you a data scientist who wants your forecasts to run every day on real energy systems — and to see the economic and carbon impact of the decisions they drive?

Join Danfoss Digital Solutions, Utility, and help build the forecasting foundation for the next generation of district energy optimization.

The Vision We Are Building Towards

District heating and cooling utilities are facing their most demanding transition yet — changing production sources, electrified heat, volatile energy markets and a hard decarbonisation mandate

Our vision is to establish a system-level optimization across production, network and demand, so that a utility can operate at the best possible energy-economic value while delivering on its decarbonisation commitments. Forecasting is playing an important role towards our vision

What You’ll Be Doing

We are looking for a Data Scientist to strengthen the forecasting capability in our Utility team. You will work on the models that tell the platform what is coming and take them from idea to production — running daily on live utility networks — closely guided by experienced data scientists who know these systems well.

Some Of The Key Activities Will Include

Build and improve energy demand forecasting models (heat and cooling load) across a growing portfolio of utility networks and get them into production with automated retraining and minimal manual intervention.
Work on local weather and condition forecasting that outperforms global and regional models at individual network level — a proven differentiator we want to push further.
Make forecasting robust at scale: self-adaptive models, drift and anomaly detection, and forecast accuracy monitoring across many networks at once.
Blend physics with data — combine physical modelling principles of thermal systems with statistical and machine learning methods, rather than treating the network as a black box.
Build and develop the data pipelines your models depend on, together with our data engineering platform team.

The Team

Your main development team is based in Denmark, working with colleagues across several European locations. Beyond your daily team, you join a data science community in Denmark of experienced data scientists working on problems next to yours — production optimization, thermo-hydraulic network simulation, temperature optimization. You will have people to think out loud with, review your models and challenge your assumptions, and you will do the same for them.

What We're Looking For

You are a data scientist who wants to turn messy real-world problems into models that work in production, and who is curious about the physical systems behind the data.

Early in your career? Please apply. We care more about how you think than how many years you have. If you are at a junior level but determined to grow into a deep specialist — rigorous about model quality, curious about how energy systems actually behave, and keen to be challenged by people who know more than you do — we want to hear from you. You will be guided closely by experienced data scientists, and we will invest in getting you there.

On top of that, you should be able to checkmark some of the points listed below:

Hold a Master’s degree or higher in a relevant field (mathematics, machine learning, statistics, physics, etc.)
PhD degree is a benefit, but not a strict requirement
Previous experience of Python as this is used as our main programming tool, together with a solid foundation in statistics and machine learning — from studies, thesis work, internships or professional experience
Experience with forecasting and time-series modelling, especially models that have to run in production
Forecasting experience in energy systems or electricity markets is a plus
Experience with modern data pipelines and cloud-based data platforms

jobs.description:
WPP is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands.

We unite cutting-edge media intelligence and data solutions, world-class creativity, next-generation production, transformative enterprise solutions and expert strategic counsel in a single company – powered by exceptional talent and our agentic marketing platform, WPP Open, to help our clients navigate change, capture opportunity and deliver transformational growth.

Our people are the key to our success. We're committed to fostering a culture of creativity, belonging and continuous learning, attracting and developing the brightest talent, and providing exciting career opportunities that help our people grow.

For more information, visit WPP.com.

Why we're hiring:

Open Intelligence (OI) is one of WPP’s most strategic bets - a flagship data and AI initiative at the intersection of machine learning, advertising technology, and audience insight, built to power the next generation of media intelligence. Operating across the US and UK and expanding across EMEA and APAC, OI runs at true global scale.

To lead the next phase of development at the embedding and applied-AI layer of OI, we are hiring a Data Science Team Lead in Copenhagen. You will guide a small, sharp team building critical capabilities - from multimodal embedding spaces and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers to agentic tools and UIs - that make the rest of OI’s AI ecosystem thrive.

What you'll be doing:

Line-manage and grow the team: Drive 1:1s, recruitment, performance, mentorship, and day-to-day technical and team direction.
Own technical architecture & direction: Lead the technical vision and design for well-distributed multimodal embedding spaces (text, image, video), MCP server tooling, and user-facing chat agents + UI.
Translate strategy into action: Take high-level, ambiguous direction from leadership and stakeholders, shape it into a clear narrative, and break it down into concrete, well-scoped projects.
Uphold a high engineering bar: Set and maintain high standards for clean architecture, system design, and testable code while keeping delivery pragmatic and incremental.
Communicate impact: Clearly articulate the team’s work, architectural decisions, and business value upward to leadership and across the wider Open Intelligence organization.
Stay hands-on: Keep close enough to the code and technical stack to make sound architectural calls, conduct code reviews, and unblock the team.

Who you'll be working with:

You’ll report directly to the Director of Data Science, Open Intelligence, and join our vibrant Copenhagen office of ~50 people, including 14+ data scientists and a strong engineering group.

We operate fluidly across closely collaborating teams. Our culture is flat, high-trust, and fast-moving: strong opinions loosely held, teamwork over ego, aiming high, and having fun along the way.

What you'll need:

Solid understanding of software architecture, system design, clean code principles, and testability. (We lean toward an engineering-minded lead, but strongly technical Data Scientists or ML Engineers with engineering instincts are very welcome).
Deep proficiency in Python and cloud experience (ideally GCP — Vertex AI, Cloud Run, BigQuery).
Hands-on experience with embeddings, vector search, LLM tooling, and agentic workflows (experience with MCP / Model Context Protocol is a strong plus).
Demonstrated ability to untangle ambiguity and turn broad goals into shipped, high-quality production systems.
Ability to shape complex technical concepts into compelling, easy-to-understand storylines for technical and non-technical stakeholders alike.

Note:
Direct people-leadership experience is a plus, but not a mandatory requirement if you have strong technical/project leadership instincts.

Success attributes:

You untangle ambiguity rather than being intimidated by it.
Pragmatic perfectionist: high standards, incremental delivery.
Low ego, high trust; you make the people around you better.
Thrive in a fast-paced, flat, entrepreneurial environment.

Who you are:

You're open :
We are inclusive and collaborative; we encourage the free exchange of ideas; we respect and celebrate diverse views. We are open-minded: to new ideas, new partnerships, new ways of working.

You're optimistic :
We believe in the power of creativity, technology and talent to create brighter futures or our people, our clients and our communities. We approach all that we do with conviction: to try the new and to seek the unexpected.

You're extraordinary:
we are stronger together: through collaboration we achieve the amazing. We are creative leaders and pioneers of our industry; we provide extraordinary every day.

What we'll give you:

Passionate, inspired people
– We aim to create a culture in which people can do extraordinary work.

Scale and opportunity
– We offer the opportunity to create, influence and complete projects at a scale that is unparalleled in the industry.

Challenging and stimulating work
– Unique work and the opportunity to join a group of creative problem solvers. Are you up for the challenge?

We believe the best work happens when we're together, fostering creativity, collaboration, and connection. That's why we’ve adopted a hybrid approach, with teams in the office around four days a week. The firm provides a comprehensive suite of services, products, and data that enable clients to navigate complex, contentious, and often catastrophic situations.

Job Description

J.S. Held is seeking a motivated and detail-oriented Environmental Scientist to join our Industrial Hygiene & Built Environment practice in Los Angeles. This role involves performing field-based environmental testing, hazardous material assessments, and supporting remediation and compliance projects across a variety of client sites.

The ideal candidate brings hands-on experience in asbestos, lead, and mold assessment, strong documentation skills, and a commitment to safety and regulatory compliance in dynamic field environments.

Job Responsibilities

Conduct on-site environmental monitoring and inspections for hazardous materials including asbestos, lead, and mold.
Perform air sampling, bulk sampling, and surface sampling in accordance with regulatory standards and project requirements.
Support indoor air quality (IAQ) assessments, including moisture mapping and environmental condition evaluations.
Complete daily field documentation, including reports, photographs, and chain-of-custody forms to maintain defensible project records.
Assist with abatement oversight, including final visual inspections and clearance air sampling.
Ensure compliance with federal, state (e.g., CDPH, OSHA), and local regulations governing hazardous materials and worker safety.
Maintain and calibrate field equipment and adhere to strict health and safety protocols.
Collaborate with project managers and industrial hygienists to support project execution and client deliverables.
Contribute to team knowledge sharing and support onboarding or training initiatives when applicable.

Required

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Industrial Hygiene, Occupational Health, Kinesiology, or related field preferred.
1 -2 years of experience in industrial hygiene, environmental consulting, or hazardous materials fieldwork.
Knowledge of asbestos, lead, and mold inspection and sampling techniques.
Familiarity with air sampling methods and laboratory coordination procedures.
Ability to work independently in the field and travel to project sites throughout the Los Angeles area.
Strong attention to detail and clear written documentation skills.
Certified Site Surveillance Technician (CSST).
Valid Driver’s License.

NIOSH 582 (or equivalent)

Push or pull items.
Able to reach above head.
Able to bend at the knee.

jobs.description:
NV5 is a provider of engineering and consulting services to public and private sector clients, delivering solutions through six business verticals: Environmental Health Sciences; Testing, Inspection & Consulting; Infrastructure; Utility Services; Buildings & Program Management; and Geospatial Technology. With offices nationwide and abroad, NV5 helps clients plan, design, build, test, certify, and operate projects that improve the communities where we live and work.

As environmental professionals, engineers, architects, construction/program managers, and beyond, we play a significant role in shaping our communities through the services we provide. We are looking for passionate, driven individuals to join our team focused on Delivering Solutions and Improving Lives .

We are seeking a Senior Water Resources/Water Quality Project Manager to join our team of Water Resources experts in Torrance, CA. This senior position is a seller-doer responsible for implementing water quality monitoring projects for municipal, industrial, and construction stormwater projects. The role involves serving as a technical expert in NPDES Permits, developing client relationships, managing project teams, and responding to client requests for proposals. The team works to serve our existing and rapidly growing client base in multiple sectors; including public agencies (Phase I and II NPDES Permittees), industrial clients (ie: aerospace, manufacturing, food service, etc.), schools and universities, and development (real estate and construction). This position is available for our Torrance, CA office and offers a remote/hybrid work setting.

Responsibilities

You are qualified for this position if you are a proven technical expert, solutions oriented, and a knowledgeable seller/doer with strong inter-personal communication skills. The ideal candidate will have a strong knowledge and background with the 2022 Construction General Stormwater Permit, southern California NPDES Permits, specifically with the Phase I-Los Angeles/Orange County/Riverside MS4 Permits. Other Phase I, Phase II, or Industrial experience is desirable or other relevant specialty, e.g., natural resources, Flood Control studies, and other related field activities, and be active in local or statewide trade agencies (e.g., CASQA, , IEA, WERF, BIA or other local environmental organizations). You have successfully led field teams and managed client relationships in the Southern California Region. Your natural leadership style fosters trust and rapport with clients, regulators and your team. You are a leader who excels in a collaborative team environment of like-minded experts and are recognized by your peers for the ability to interpret technical and analytical data and present it in a clear concise and understandable reports and graphics for clients (and the layperson). You will promote our brand and build business through interaction with prospects and clients, high quality work, publications, and technical presentations.

Key Responsibilities will include:

Executing specialized water quality and water quantity studies, special studies, and regulatory compliance interpretations and implementation services.
Preparing Sampling and Analysis Plans, Quality Assurance Project Plans, and other relevant technical reports.
Managing industrial, construction, and/or municipal agency NPDES monitoring and reporting projects.
Growing client relationships through consultative technical sales to develop projects and drive business growth.
Performing regulatory compliance services and permit acquisition.
Leading and mentoring technical staff to help them grow their careers as expert
Interfacing directly with technical leads and clients to determine service needs for developing technical proposals (scope, costs, schedule, and budgets).
Responsible for quality control review of proposals and reports written by others.

Qualifications

The ideal candidate will possess the following qualifications and skills:

Bachelor’s, Master’s, or Ph.D degree from an accredited university in civil/environmental/ chemical engineering or related sciences field and at least 7+ years of demonstrated consulting experience in Southern California.
Storm water industry certifications are required (e.g., CPSWQ or CPESC and QSD).
Strong understanding of the 2022 Construction General Stormwater Permit and the Los Angeles Phase I NPDES Permit. Other Phase I MS4 permit knowledge in southern California is desirable.
Extensive experience with water quality monitoring equipment (autosamplers, water quality meters, flow monitoring, data loggers, remote telemetry, innovative use of novel monitoring devices).
Strong operational use of computer databases and office programs (MS Access, MS Excel, MS Word).
Strong oral and written communication skills; ability to prepare reports and proposals.
Excellent writing and analytical skills a must.
Project team management oversight and leadership ability.

The pay range for this California position is $120,000- $150,000 per year; however, base pay offered may be higher or lower depending on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience of the candidate. Restricted stock units may be provided as part of the compensation package, in addition to a full range of medical, financial, and/or other benefits, dependent on the position offered. This information is provided per California Senate Bill 1162. Base pay information is based on market location. Applicants should apply via the NV5 careers site.

jobs.title: Drinking Water Business Development Director
jobs.description:
At HDR, our employee-owners are fully engaged in creating a welcoming environment where each of us is valued and respected, a place where everyone is empowered to bring their authentic selves and novel ideas to work every day. As we foster a culture of inclusion throughout our company and within our communities, we constantly ask ourselves: What is our impact on the world?

Watch Our Story:' https://www.hdrinc.com/our-story'

Each and every role throughout our organization makes a difference in our ability to change the world for the better. Read further to learn how you could help make great things possible not only in your community, but around the world.

The Drinking Water Market Sector (“MS”) Business Development Director (BDD) will lead the development and implementation of business strategies across all HDR geographies in coordination with Market Sector and Regional Business Group leadership, operational leadership, client managers and Business Class Directors.   Reporting to the Director of Market Sector Development, and in full coordination with the Water Business Group leadership, the Drinking Water BDD creates and monitors frequent and regular communication across the Sector to drive top-line NFB growth and to implement the Drinking Water sector’s strategic initiatives, growth plans and marketing opportunities for the market sector. This market leader will support and collaborate across all HDR market sectors, regions, areas and business lines to advance a variety of strategies intended to grow services across the market sector. 

Drinking Water Market Sector–
Within the Water Business Group, the Drinking Water MS is a highly technical and diversified sector.  This reflects that this service offering routinely works for local municipalities, private entities, distinct water utilities, Federal, regional and local governments, and similar clients in each of the 50 US states, Canada, the United Kingdom and Australia.  In 2026 Engineering News Record ranked HDR fifth in size of business in the important water supply and treatment category.  We have over 475 employees in this MS spanning the range of services from utility master planning, program management, strategic advisory services, transmission and distribution, water supply management, water treatment and reuse, construction management and inspection, and asset management and operations assistance.

The Drinking Water MS is comprised of a multi-layer organization to drive business and client development, while at the same time defining and implementing strategic drinking water initiatives for growth, coordinating best practices and quality professional services, and projecting the HDR brand in the marketplace.  Specific attention is required to capture the potential of the wide spectrum of employees throughout the Sector, while at the same time developing and reinforcing the image of HDR with our clients across the various drinking water markets.  

Business Development Responsibilities
 – The Drinking Water Market Sector BDD primary performance metric is achieving NFB goals for the sector. You will provide leadership and substantial support to assessing the Regional and Area marketplace positioning and determining optimal technical strategies needed to win and secure contracts and expand business. Business development efforts will extend across all business groups to coordinate with other Architecture, Transportation, Resources, Water, BES and Federal Business Group market sectors.  This position will implement cross sector initiatives including One Water, the Value of Water, and other Sector strategies that are effective in gaining market share, and that will successfully interface with Regional/Area client development programs, our Strategic Pursuits program, and Regional/Area marketing managers/pursuit leaders. Specific business development activities include:

Incorporate our HDR and Water business vision within the market sector to become the industry leader.

Serve as the Client Manager for selected key clients within the Sector and be active and visible in the industry.

Serve as Pursuit Leader on select drinking water opportunities, leading by example in the development of pursuit strategies, proposal development and interview preparation.

Work with client managers to promote the marketing and delivery of all HDR services to Drinking Water clients across all HDR geographies.

Participate as a member of the Water Business Group Management and the National Drinking Water Market Sector Leadership Team support the coordinated development of international markets in Canada, the United Kingdom and Australia, in support of broader Water Business Group international growth initiatives. Work with Regional Business Group Managers and Client Development Leadership in the development and delivery of MS initiatives that align with area and regional drivers.

Work with the client development leaders to support client development, deploy pursuit strategies, and guide pursuit processes, based on proven capture techniques.

Provide direct support to selected pursuits through client relationship development and/or through development of strategy, technical differentiation, and participation in related pursuit activities.

Actively participate in industry associations in leadership roles and serve as a company role-model in business and community organizations.

Identify key investments (acquisitions and technology) that will maintain or drive HDR into an industry leadership position.

Maintain awareness of Area marketing capabilities and provide market sector support to Areas toward achieving Drinking Water MS booking goals. 

Develop relationships with industry counterparts in other consulting and construction organizations. 

Develop relationships with senior leadership in key client organizations.

Staff Development Responsibilities
 – The Drinking Water MS BDD will seek opportunities to enhance our performance to win new work within the marketplace and provide opportunities for staff growth and development.  Through pursuit leadership and involvement, strategically align Drinking Water staff and projects to develop and deepen skills, while mentoring and growing their capabilities and talent. Lead and/or assist with the identification and recruitment of prospective future market sector employees.

Work with the Drinking Water MS leader, Business Class Directors, and practice groups to drive technical excellence and coordinate technical staff to promote quality delivery and our Drive to Zero initiative. 

Coordinate staffing/recruiting plans for key hires and assist local leadership as necessary with local hires. Identify resource gaps and support talent management and recruiting.

Support to Key Project/Program Delivery –
 The Drinking Water MS BDD will assist Regional and Area Business Group leadership in key project delivery within the market sector.  Key responsibilities consist of helping to drive client management, acting as Principal in Charge on key project delivery, and supporting the QA/QC program to provide for successful project delivery. Facilitate cooperation and eliminate hurdles and barriers to success. Work with a business group leadership to implement process improvements and leverage work sharing to meet or exceed planned goals.

Be aware of staff workload and facilitate work sharing within the market sector; promote effective use of company resources and assist in applying key staff/expertise to projects. 

Assist with contract review on key projects to help ensure risk management, proper staffing, quality reviews and resolution of claims.

Take on Principal in Charge assignments that leverage this leadership role by driving client satisfaction, staff development, technical excellence and mentoring opportunities.

Preferred Qualifications

Minimum 20 + years of experience in drinking water planning and engineering design, client development, and project management; much of that experience must reside within servicing of drinking water public and private clients and utilities.
Minimum of a bachelor’s degree in an accredited civil or environmental engineering program.
Maintain a professional engineering registration.
Experienced in development and management of strategic positioning and technical differentiation for planning and/or engineering services.
Experienced in development and management of a wide range of client relationships and specific program and/or project pursuits.
Experienced in overall staff development to include recruiting, career path development, and professional growth.
Experienced with industry associations and maintains an active and visible profile in the market sector.
Ability to work cooperatively with Market Sector Directors, Business Class Directors, Regional Business Group Director, Area Business Group Managers, Area Marketing Managers and Area Manager.
Demonstrated commitment to HDR values. An attitude and commitment to being an active participant of our employee-owned culture is a must.

Required Qualifications

A minimum of 15 years relevant industry experience
Demonstrated "self-starter" with a history of completing projects with limited oversight
Deep knowledge of the A/E/C industry's standard approach to procurement of professional services
Demonstrated ability to motivate and inspire others
Demonstrated ability to build a network of clients and industry partners
Experience in sales and developing effective win strategies
Strong financial acumen and negotiation skills
Excellent written and verbal communication skills
Proficient in Microsoft Office applications, including Outlook, Word, Excel and PowerPoint
Ability and desire to travel and engage with others in-person
Demonstrated experience in growing programs in new or highly competitive markets
Demonstrated experience in winning high-value contracts in the A/E/C industry
Demonstrated experience in writing compelling content based on information from technical staff

What We Believe

HDR is our company. Together, we build on each other's life experiences and perspectives to make great things possible every day. This shapes our collaborative culture, encourages organizational trust and connects us closer to the clients and communities we serve.

[Accepting submissions until 8/28. Position description has been modified to meet word count, please visit our website for full description and application link]

Cannabis for Conservation (CFC) is a 501(c)(3) environmental nonprofit that conserves, restores, and educates rural landowners with ecological tools and resources. We turn yesterday's impacts into tomorrow's solutions. From eroding roads to fire-prone forests and from exhausted soils to struggling salmon-bearing streams, we partner with cultivators, landowners, and communities to restore functional and biodiverse agroecosystems, protect clean water, and strengthen resilience to wildfire and climate change.

We are seeking to hire a Watershed Specialist with a strong field background and several years of professional experience in geology, hydrology, environmental science, forestry, civil engineering, natural resources, and project coordination. This role will strengthen CFC's ability to assess rural roads and watershed conditions, develop conceptual sediment reduction treatments, and support implementation across Humboldt, Trinity, and Mendocino Counties. The right candidate will understand how soil, water, gravity, and rural roads interact on steep, wet landscapes, how to work with a variety of stakeholders including rural landowners, a diverse organizational staff, funders, and agency representatives.

To apply, please read the full position description and application process on our website
(www.cannabisforconservation.org/careers) by clicking the "Apply" button above and submitting your materials through the application linked on our site. Questions or issues with the application process may be sent to: vanessa@cannabisforconservation.org.

Position Overview

The Watershed Specialist supports CFC’s watershed restoration and sediment reduction projects through field assessment, planning, and project and partner coordination. Core duties include assessing rural and forest roads to identify erosion and sediment sources, estimating sediment loads, evaluating hydrologic connectivity, and developing treatment recommendations. The role combines field work with office-based reporting, permitting support, and coordination with staff, landowners, and subcontractors.

This position typically works across several concurrent, landscape-scale, multi-year, multi-parcel grant projects — helping track deliverables and milestones, keep technical and field components aligned with grant requirements, and support communication with landowners and subcontractors. The Specialist also supports engineering design through field data collection and contributes to implementation through construction oversight and inspections, in collaboration with the Watershed Program Manager and the contracted Engineer of Record.

This is not an entry-level position
. The successful candidate will bring several years of relevant field-based experience in road assessment, sediment reduction, and watershed restoration planning.

Required Skills

Bachelor’s degree in geology, hydrology, civil engineering, environmental science, forestry, natural resources, or a related field
5+ years of relevant professional experience in restoration, forestry, hydrology, geology, or a related field
Strong technical background and applicable field skills; ability to conduct field assessments of roads, culverts, ditch relief features, gullies, and other erosion and sediment sources, applying strong field assessment skills to identify erosion processes, drainage patterns, hydrologic connectivity, and sediment delivery mechanisms
Collect GPS points/tracks, photos, and field sketches using ArcGIS Field Maps, and apply basic working knowledge of ArcGIS for data collection and assessment
Evaluate planning-level feasibility of standard rural road treatments (rolling dips, outsloping/insloping, critical dips, ditch relief culverts, rock armoring, culvert sizing for fish passage and 100-year flow) and apply erosion hazard rating criteria to prioritize treatment sites
Working knowledge of watercourse classification (Class I/II/III perennial, intermittent, and ephemeral streams) and its permitting implications
Familiarity with the Handbook for Forest Ranch and Rural Roads (Pacific Watershed Associates) and road-related sediment source inventory / erosion hazard rating methodologies
Familiarity with the regulatory permitting landscape — including CDFW Lake and Streambed Alteration Agreements (LSAA), Regional Water Board 401 certification / Rural Roads General Order, and CEQA — and the ability to support integration of these considerations into planning and permitting documents
Translate field observations into treatment recommendations and prescriptions; draft technical sections of work plans, conceptual design plans, reports, permits, and other planning documents
Work with GIS staff to refine treatments, establish biological buffers, and define construction staging areas; prepare simple diagrams or sketches of conceptual treatments
Participate in internal design reviews and represent CFC in multi-agency Design Advisory Team / Technical Advisory Committee and partner meetings (e.g., CDFW, Regional Water Board, Resource Conservation Districts)
Strong knowledge of Northern California ecosystems and environmental issues
Track tasks, field schedules, and deliverables across multiple concurrent grants (e.g., in Asana), and maintain organized project files, notes, and photos
Strong coordination skills; ability to coordinate with landowners, contractors, biological and GIS staff, and the Engineer of Record
Strong and clear communication (written and verbal) skills; experience working with private landowners, subcontractors, and interdisciplinary project teams; support the Watershed Program Director with planning, logistics, and documentation
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple project sites, workstreams, and timelines simultaneously — sequencing field assessments, permitting milestones, and construction across landscape-scale, multi-year, multi-parcel projects, each with distinct funder deadlines and reporting requirements
Prioritize treatment sites across an entire road network or watershed based on erosion hazard, sediment delivery potential, and funding constraints
Track cumulative outcomes (e.g., sediment reduced, road miles treated, crossings upgraded) and assist with funder progress reports
Self-directed problem-solving ability, sound judgment, and adaptability in unfamiliar field situations
Strong ability to take initiative and contribute meaningfully to project work
Proficiency with Google Workspace, Microsoft Office, and Adobe PDF Reader
Valid driver’s license; willingness to use a personal vehicle for field travel intermittently (mileage reimbursed at the current GSA rate) and to travel overnight (Note: field vehicles are available through CFC, but on occasion personal vehicle use for field work may be requested)
Ability to operate 4WD vehicles and work safely and navigate in steep, remote, rugged terrain for full 10-hour field days, often without cell service
Ability to hike steep, uneven, and sometimes muddy or overgrown terrain for extended periods, carrying field gear for a full field day
Ability to work outdoors in variable weather conditions, including rain, heat, and cold
Comfortable with exposure to poison oak, ticks, and other common backcountry hazards
Willingness to be adaptive, a team player, and cross-trained in tasks as part of a scaling organization

Desired Qualifications

Master’s degree in geology, hydrology, civil engineering, environmental science, forestry, rangeland science, or a similar field
Deep familiarity with Northern California landscapes and environmental history, particularly Humboldt, Trinity, or Mendocino counties
Additional experience in aquatic biology, soil science, forest management, or another environmental science field
Strong understanding of permitting processes through CDFW, Regional Water Board, and county agencies
Established relationships with regional NGOs, watershed organizations, and public agencies
Wilderness First Aid/CPR certification (willingness to obtain is required if not already certified)
Familiarity with task management software (e.g., Asana) for task tracking

Location and Work Environment

This position is based out of CFC's office in the Glendale area of Blue Lake, California. The Specialist must reside in or be willing to relocate to the North Coast region and be available for frequent in-person fieldwork across Humboldt, Trinity, and Mendocino Counties.

This is not a remote position
. While some flexible or partial work-from-home scheduling is possible, regular fieldwork, team meetings, and partner coordination require consistent on-site presence.

Compensation

This is a full time, hourly, non-exempt position eligible for overtime, with a compensation range of $40–53 per hour, commensurate with experience, and annual 3% performance-based raises.

Benefits

Benefits include:
Two weeks paid vacation plus federal holidays (vacation accrual increases with tenure)
Weekly flex-time, flexible scheduling, and work-from-home options
Paid sick leave and bereavement leave
Three months full-paid parental leave and a monthly childcare stipend for employees who have worked for the organization for one year
Healthcare coverage (Anthem Blue Cross)
403(b) retirement plan (2026 match amount pending)
Opportunities for paid professional development

jobs.description:
Protecting the Individual, the Public, and the Environment

Responsibilities

The Department of Resource Management is a comprehensive agency comprised of the Environmental Health Services, Building and Safety, Planning Services, Public Works, Parks and Administrative Services Divisions. The department provides for the well-being of Solano County's present and future residents and the public at-large through administration and enforcement of Federal, State, and Local laws and policies pertaining to environmental health, building construction, land use planning, transportation and recreation. The Environmental Health Services Division is responsible for protecting public health and the environment by implementing environmental health programs in three broad areas:

The Consumer Protection Program, which includes food facilities, pools & spas, body art, and public events
The Technical Services Program, which includes drinking water wells, septic systems, and solid waste handling and disposal
The Hazardous Materials Program, which includes aboveground and underground storage tanks, hazardous materials & hazardous waste management, and emergency response.

Click here to learn more about the Department of Resource Management

THE POSITION

The Environmental Health Specialist (Senior) performs the more complex and specialized work in the regulation and enforcement of Environmental Health and Safety laws and regulations; assists with planning and implementation of specialized programs and projects within the Environmental Health Division to assure compliance with Federal, State, and local health and safety codes and requirements; may lead by providing training and guidance to entry and journey level staff within the Environmental Health Division; conducts inspections and investigations, reviews plans for conformance with health and safety code requirements, and processes permits; performs related duties as required.

The eligible list established from this recruitment will be used to fill full-time and part-time regular, limited-term or extra-help positions as vacancies occur or the need arises.

Education And Experience Requirements

Experience:

Three (3) years of experience in Environmental Health and Safety regulation and enforcement; considerable and responsible experience directly related to the specific program assignment.

AND

Education/Training:

A Bachelor’s degree, from an accredited four-year college or university, which meets the requirements of the California Health and Safety Code, Division 104, Part 1, Chapter 4, Article 1, Section 106600 (et sequiter).

Other Requirements

Must be registered with the State of California as Registered Environmental Health Specialist, in accordance with Division 104, Part 1, Chapter 4, Article 1, Section 106600 (et sequiter) of the California Health and Safety Code.
Possession of or the ability to obtain a valid Class C California driver’s license.

to join our Global Regulatory Affairs team at our headquarters in Bend, Oregon.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone early in their regulatory or environmental compliance career who wants to gain hands-on experience working with federal and state regulatory requirements, environmental reporting, and product compliance in a collaborative manufacturing environment.

You'll work closely with Manufacturing, Operations, Quality, R&D, Supply Chain, and Commercial teams to help ensure our products and operations remain compliant while supporting innovative technologies used around the world.

This position is based full-time in Bend, Oregon. Regular onsite collaboration is an essential part of this role. Remote or hybrid work arrangements are not available. Relocation to the Bend area is required for candidates who do not currently reside locally.

Job Description

What You'll Do

As a Regulatory & Environmental Compliance Analyst, you'll support the day-to-day regulatory and environmental compliance activities that keep our products, facilities, and operations running safely and responsibly.

Responsibilities include:

Prepare and maintain environmental reports required by federal, state, and local regulatory agencies.
Support environmental permitting and compliance activities, including waste management, air emissions, hazardous materials, and chemical reporting.
Assist with regulatory submissions, product registrations, renewals, and regulatory documentation.
Maintain permits, certifications, regulatory files, and compliance records.
Monitor changes in environmental and regulatory requirements and communicate potential impacts to the business.
Support regulatory inspections, agency requests, and internal and external audits.
Partner with Manufacturing, Quality, R&D, Supply Chain, and Operations to ensure regulatory requirements are incorporated into daily operations.
Assist in developing compliance procedures, documentation, and employee training materials.
Identify opportunities to improve regulatory processes and strengthen compliance programs.

Qualifications

What We're Looking For

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Environmental Science, Biology, Chemistry, Environmental Engineering, Natural Resources, or a related scientific field.
Approximately 2–5 years of experience in environmental compliance, regulatory affairs, EHS, environmental consulting, manufacturing compliance, or a related field.
Experience working with or preparing documentation for federal and/or state regulatory agencies such as EPA, OSHA, DEQ, ODA, or similar agencies.
Experience supporting environmental reporting, permitting, inspections, or compliance documentation.
Strong organizational skills with exceptional attention to detail.
Ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining accurate records and documentation.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in manufacturing, agriculture, chemical manufacturing, biotechnology, food production, or related industries.
Familiarity with pesticide, chemical, or environmental regulations.
Experience participating in regulatory inspections or compliance audits.

You'll Be Successful in This Role If You

Enjoy working with technical regulations and detailed documentation.
Like solving practical problems and finding compliant solutions.
Can build positive working relationships across multiple departments.
Are organized, dependable, and proactive.
Want to continue building your expertise in environmental and regulatory compliance.
Appreciate working in a collaborative, onsite environment.

Additional Information

Why Join Suterra?

This is more than a field service role. It's the first step in a career supporting growers, advancing sustainable agriculture, and developing technical expertise in one of California's most important industries.

At Suterra, you'll receive:

Hands-on training and mentorship from experienced agricultural professionals.
Opportunities to build technical skills and grow your career.
The chance to work with innovative technology that's making agriculture more sustainable.
Competitive salary and comprehensive benefits.
A collaborative team that values curiosity, integrity, and continuous learning.

If you're passionate about agriculture, enjoy working outdoors, and are ready to grow your career, we'd love to hear from you.

Suterra Is Wholly Owned By The Wonderful Company

The Wonderful Company, headquartered in Los Angeles, is a privately held $6 billion global agribusiness company with consumer brands including Wonderful® Pistachios, Wonderful® Halos®, POM Wonderful®, FIJI® Water, JUSTIN® and Landmark® wines, as well as the Teleflora® flower delivery service.

To learn more about The Wonderful Company, visit www.wonderful.com, or follow us on Facebook, Twitter and Instagram. To view the current Corporate Social Responsibility report, visit www.wonderful.com/csr.

jobs.description:
About Us

At the County of Marin, our employees overwhelmingly report feeling their work is meaningful, they like the work they do, and they are proud to tell people “I work for the County of Marin.” Discover more about us, our values and our organizational culture on the Department of Human Resources website. Read on to find out more about this opportunity.

The Community Development Agency (CDA) has a long history of innovation and leadership. CDA is a multifunctional agency shaping many aspects of environment and communities, organized into five mission-oriented divisions: Planning, Building and Safety, Environmental Health Services, Housing and Federal Grants, and Sustainability. CDA’s mission is to promote, protect, and advance healthy, safe, and equitable communities.

Environmental Health Services is a Division in the Community Development Agency:
The mission of Marin County Environmental Health Services is to protect public health and the well-being of all Marin County residents, workers, and visitors by preventing injury and the spread of disease. We identify potentially dangerous and unhealthy situations and promote sound environmental health practices through education and the enforcement of public health statutes and regulations.

About The Position

The Senior Environmental Health Specialist (SEHS) acts as the lead and the subject matter expert in their assigned program. For the current vacancy, the SEHS will focus heavily on plan check operations, conducting comprehensive reviews of building and architectural plans, and performing critical preliminary and final construction field inspections to ensure projects meet environmental health standards. This role requires the ability to successfully manage a high volume of plan check submittals under tight, time-sensitive agency deadlines.

In addition to plan review, the SEHS performs general environmental health duties. They serve as a consumer protection and food safety expert responsible for understanding and interpreting complex regulations and guidelines. They possess in-depth knowledge of foodborne illnesses and outbreaks, effectively educating staff and the public. Across all Consumer Protection program areas, the SEHS will conduct general inspections, investigate complaints, represent the County to the community and business owners, assist management with code interpretation, help develop department policies, and work closely with local and state officials to gain compliance. Please note that overtime, night, and weekend work is required for events permit enforcement.

Fixed-Term:

This is a three (3) Year fixed-term position.

This position is budgeted for three (3) Years. However, there may be opportunities for the hired individual during this time-period to move to a regular, ongoing position as other vacancies or promotional opportunities occur, or the position may be funded and convert to an ongoing position. Fixed-term employment ends when the position’s funding finishes, or the work is completed. Employees in these positions are exempt from the County’s policies regarding lay-off order and reduction-in-force rights.

About You

The Highly Qualified Candidate
possesses technical experience reviewing commercial building plans, interpreting architectural or engineering schematics, and conducting construction-phase field inspections. They have experience handling a large volume of plan submissions while consistently hitting strict turnaround times. Additionally, the ideal candidate possesses strong general knowledge and field experience in consumer protection and other environmental health programs. They are highly organized, customer-focused, and possess superior conflict resolution and communication skills (both oral and written). This individual effectively utilizes technology for record-keeping and research, works well with outside agencies, exhibits a passion for environmental health, and has a strong commitment to public health. Experience leading a program and/or staff is a plus.

Knowledge Of:

Our Highly Qualified Candidate has:

Principles and practices of architectural plan review, equipment specifications, and construction materials for commercial and food facilities.
Building, plumbing, and mechanical codes as they interface with environmental health standards and design layouts.
Scientific principles of biology, chemistry, and environmental science used to evaluate public health risks and maintain environmental sanitation standards.
Roles and procedures of external agencies such as building, fire, and sanitary districts as they interface with environmental health approvals and clearances.
Statutes, regulations, and local ordinances governing environmental health, public health safety, and retail food facility compliance.
State and local laws governing the definition, enforcement, and correction of public health nuisances.
Methods and techniques for identifying public health risk factors, conducting regulatory inspections, and enforcing compliance to eliminate environmental hazards.
Techniques for managing competing priorities, maintaining accurate regulatory records, and meeting strict agency deadlines
Advanced problem-solving and conflict resolution techniques used to navigate complex regulatory disputes, de-escalate tense field situations, and guide uncooperative builders or operators toward voluntary code compliance.
Ability to successfully navigate permit tracking software and utilize standard computer applications, including word processing and email systems.

Ability To:

Review, interpret, and evaluate complex architectural plans, blueprints, equipment specifications, and construction materials for commercial and food facilities to ensure compliance.
Identify discrepancies where building, plumbing, and mechanical codes intersect or conflict with environmental health standards and facility design layouts.
Apply scientific principles of biology, chemistry, and environmental science to accurately assess public health risks and formulate data-driven solutions for environmental sanitation standards.
Coordinate and streamline cross-agency clearances, maintaining effective working relationships with building officials, fire inspectors, sanitary district, and other agency personnel.
Analyze regulatory situations accurately and take effective enforcement action based on state statutes, local health ordinances, and retail food facility regulations.
Investigate and document public health nuisances, prepare legally sound reports, and execute formal enforcement or abatement procedures.
Conduct rigorous field inspections to detect unsanitary conditions, identify risk factors, and secure mandatory corrections using specialized investigative techniques.
Manage, prioritize, and track a high volume of plan check submittals and competing project deadlines while maintaining meticulous regulatory records in digital permit software.
Employ advanced communication, mediation, and de-escalation strategies to handle tense field situations, resolve complex regulatory disputes, and guide uncooperative builders or operators toward voluntary compliance.
Instruct, mentor, and coach staff, business owners, and the public on complex environmental health inspection methods, code interpretations, and correction procedures.

QUALIFICATIONS

Knowledge Of:

Basic principles of physical, biological and sciences used in environmental sanitation.
Functions and operation of related agencies.
State and local laws and regulations governing public health.
Penal code provisions relating to public health nuisances.
Methods and techniques of investigation, inspection and resolving unsanitary conditions.
General principles and practices of environmental health.
Principles and techniques of organization.
Environmental research and statistical methods.
Design of research studies such as data sources and collection methods necessary to obtain information on various public health and sanitation programs and problems.
Principles and techniques of problem solving and conflict resolution.
Basic computer applications including word processing and e-mail computer systems (depending upon assignment, more may be required).

Ability To:

Analyze situations accurately and take effective action.
Prepare clear and concise reports and letters.
Plan, organize and carry out research.
Analyze and evaluate data and make recommendations based on findings.
Detect unsanitary conditions and public health hazards and secure their correction through education, voluntary compliance or legal enforcement.
Instruct in the methods and procedures of environmental health inspections and correction of said conditions.
Apply knowledge of a specialized and complex nature.
Interpret public health needs and goals to others.
Work effectively with issues in which there are inherent tensions and conflicts.
Communicate and interact in situations requiring instruction, persuasion, coaching.
Meet and deal effectively with the public and help in resolving conflicts and solving problems.
Establish and maintain effective working relationships with those contacted in the course of the work.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

Two (2) years of full-time environmental health experience performing duties equivalent to a Registered Environmental Health Specialist which demonstrates possession of the listed knowledge and abilities.

One (1) year of experience working in the Environmental Health and Safety field in California is required.

A graduate degree from an accredited college or university with a major in Public Health, Health Science, Business Administration, Public Administration or a related field is highly desirable.

Certificates and Licenses

Possession of a valid certificate of registration as an Environmental Health Specialist with the California Department of Public Health.
