**This Opportunity**
--------------------

WSP is currently initiating a search for an Early Career Environmental Scientist for our Vancouver, WA Office. Takes part in providing local technical assistance for the collection, identification, and compiling of observational and spatial data concerning a variety of biological, physical, and earth sciences. Provides local assistance for the development of processes and infrastructure relating to water supply, air emission, pollution control, cultural impact, and preserving the quality of the environment by identifying, controlling, and preventing disruption to environmental systems and species caused by human activity. Generates accurate and concise documentation, ensuring that responsibilities are delivered and adhered to with a level of quality that meets or exceeds acceptable industry standards.


**Your Impact**
---------------

* Under general supervision, conduct natural resource field surveys collecting observational, spatial, and environmental data.

* Maintain quality control standards and procedures for accurate and precise measurement and documentation.

jobs.description:
At Jacobs, we're challenging today to reinvent tomorrow by solving the world's most critical problems for thriving cities, resilient environments, mission-critical outcomes, operational advancement, scientific discovery and cutting-edge manufacturing, turning abstract ideas into realities that transform the world for good.

Your impact

At Jacobs, we push the limits of what’s possible to make the world more connected and sustainable. For our radiation services community of practice, that means using innovative approaches to provide economical client solutions for complex environmental solutions. We’re seeking a Radiation Health Physicist to support projects for primarily our US Navy and uranium mining restoration clients, though our portfolio is broad, and many other clients and projects are included. We also want to grow and develop your career with task and project management.

Projects will involve a variety of field implementations for radiological assessments and remediation, plan development, data evaluation, desktop research and document reviews. Must have experience in environmental projects that evaluate soil, groundwater, surface water, or sediments. Projects could be executed under EPA, NRC, Agreement States, USACE, or Tribal Agency authority and may include investigations, risk assessments, feasibility studies, engineering analysis, remedial actions, and closures.

It is expected that field tasks would be required and may include performing and/or leading teams during surveys and assessments. Additionally, characterizing radiological materials in various matrices, implementing radiation safety practices, maintaining radiation protection programs, and regulatory compliance during project activities.

A balance of remote and office work is expected, and preference will be given to candidates located in Virginia, California, or Colorado.

The position offers the opportunity to elevate your Health Physics career working with and being mentored by the highly professional, experienced, and credentialed Jacobs radiation services staff on a wide variety of health physics related issues. Opportunities for leadership and ownership on projects is expected and developing technical and project management skills will be further developed. Writing clearly, presenting technical approaches, and justifying decisions are essential, as we help clients obtain regulatory and community acceptance and close projects.

Bring your curiosity, collaborative attitude, desire for leadership, to our team and we’ll help you grow. We will help you pursue and fulfill what drives you – so we can improve lives together.

Here's what you'll need

B.S. degree in Radiation Health Physics or Nuclear Engineering.
Experience with Navy environmental and remediation programs.
Radiation safety officer experience.

Ideally, You’ll Also Have

M.S. in Health Physics or Nuclear Engineering.
CHP, American Board of Health Physics Certification.
10 to 15 Years Professional Health Physics Experience
Experience with CERCLA projects
Experience radiological investigations or BRAC closures.
Project management experience.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or protected veteran status. Job posted on August 14, 2026. This position will be open for at least 3 days.

jobs.title: Environmental Scientist
jobs.description:
The Opportunity

Tetra Tech is adding an Environmental Scientist
to our water resources environmental team based in Portland, OR.

Why Tetra Tech

At Tetra Tech, we are  Leading with Science  to solve the world’s most complex challenges. Our industry-leading experts in engineering and consulting are committed to driving positive change in communities around the world. For 60 years, we have been at the forefront of innovation and sustainability. Today we stand as a market leader, offering cutting-edge solutions in water, environment, energy, and international development. Our work has improved more than 625 million lives around the world.

Your Impact

Join Tetra Tech to make a real difference. Our work leverages cutting-edge technologies, advanced analytics, and the expertise of world-class scientists and engineers to create meaningful change around the world. Discover your full potential – join us to advance your career while leaving  a lasting legacy .

Position Summary

We’re currently seeking an Environmental Scientist
to join our team of biologists, environmental planners, and engineers who specialize in aquatic habitat restoration, biological studies, environmental assessments, permit applications, and NEPA documentation for projects throughout the West Coast and Alaska. Our team has worked on several exciting and impactful projects, including:

Environmental review of an 800,000-acre-foot groundwater bank in California
Wetland restoration on islands in the Columbia River
Salton Sea Restoration Project
Endangered Species Act / Marine Mammal Protection Act compliance for U.S. Coast Guard bases in Alaska and the west coast
Wildlife monitoring on the Santa Ana River
Permitting fish passage restoration projects in Washington

This position offers diverse project types and clear opportunities for professional growth and advancement within the firm.

Essential Job Functions

The following duties are essential to this role. Reasonable accommodation will be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these functions. 

Prepare, review, and analyze environmental documentation under NEPA, SEPA, and CEQA processes.
Prepare Endangered Species Act (ESA) compliance documentation, including technical reports and field-based assessments.
Conduct field surveys related to vegetation, wildlife habitat, and riverine features throughout the Pacific Northwest.
Perform GIS mapping and data analysis to support project planning, environmental review, and reporting.
Conduct wetland delineations in accordance with applicable methodologies and regulatory standards.
Apply wetland and stream rapid assessment methodologies in California, Oregon, and Washington.
Prepare and oversee the development of environmental permits, including Clean Water Act Sections 404 and 401 permits.
Support stream and wetland restoration planning and implementation activities.
Perform task management and assist project management for complex environmental projects.
Assist with business development efforts related to biological and environmental services.

Requirements / Qualifications

Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Biology , Geography, Environmental Sciences, Water Resources Sciences, or a related field .
Minimum of 5 years of professional experience in environmental sciences, including NEPA, permitting, GIS, surveying, water quality, and wetland delineations.
Demonstrated knowledge of local plant , fish, and/or wildlife species and their habitat requirements.

jobs.title: Environmental Risk Assessor
jobs.description:
SLR Consulting (Canada) is a team of more than 800+ advisory, environmental, engineering, and regulatory professionals working across 18 offices nationwide. By integrating advisory services with over 30 technical environmental and engineering disciplines, we help clients navigate complex environmental challenges and advance their sustainability goals.

At SLR, our work supports better environmental outcomes for communities, ecosystems, and industry. Together with our clients, we are committed to Making Sustainability Happen.

As our newest Environmental Risk Assessor
, you will play an important role in supporting this mission.

Working within our national Risk Assessment team, you will contribute to a variety of complex environmental projects while applying your regulatory knowledge and continuing to expand your expertise in provincial and federal requirements. In this role, you will collaborate closely with internal teams, clients, and regulators to develop technical scopes of work, prepare proposals, and support the successful management and delivery of projects.

This role offers exceptional opportunities for professional growth, providing the chance to work on projects from coast to coast and collaborate with experienced teams across North America, all while gaining exposure to a wide range of regulatory frameworks, environmental challenges, and consulting practices. Working on complex, multidisciplinary projects across sectors such as mining, oil and gas, land development, and federal, provincial, territorial, and municipal jurisdictions will allow you to continually deepen your technical expertise. You’ll also gain valuable experience navigating emerging contaminants and engaging with diverse stakeholders, including regulators, Indigenous communities, industry partners, and the general public. This variety will not only strengthen your technical foundation, but accelerate your development as a well‑rounded environmental professional capable of leading in dynamic and evolving practice areas.

Our team is passionate about delivering high-quality work and building strong client relationships. We are looking for someone who shares this mindset and brings strong communication skills, attention to detail, and the ability to manage competing priorities in a dynamic consulting environment. Success in this role will require flexibility, independence, and a commitment to delivering high-quality technical work.

Specific Responsibilities Will Include

Develop and deliver human health and ecological risk assessments, risk management plans, performance verification plans, etc. in accordance with provincial, territorial, and federal regulatory frameworks
Support proposal development, including contributing to project scoping, planning, and budgeting activities.
Evaluate site-specific physical characteristics, environmental data, receptor exposure assumptions, and toxicity information to inform the development of exposure and risk models.
Prepare detailed conceptual site models by consolidating and interpreting field data, laboratory results, and other relevant site and receptor information.
Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams to prepare high-quality technical reports and effectively communicate findings to clients, regulators, and other stakeholders.
Contribute to proposal writing and provide technical support to projects led by other disciplines, such as site assessment and ecology.
Mentor and support junior staff, fostering skill development and knowledge sharing within the team.

Working @ SLR

At SLR, we believe in investing in our people for the long term. Our team members continue to grow their subject-matter expertise while working on meaningful projects that make a real impact. We aim to create an environment where you can build a rewarding and sustainable career.

What You Can Expect

Meaningful project work supporting complex environmental and sustainability challenges across Canada
Opportunities to collaborate with multidisciplinary teams across more than 30 environmental and engineering disciplines
Support for technical specialization, project management development, and leadership growth
A collaborative culture where knowledge sharing and mentorship are encouraged

Our Benefits

Comprehensive benefits, vacation, RRSP and a suite of wellness initiatives
Salary range: $75,000 – $115,000 Final agreed upon compensation will reflect education, professional designation, experience, internal parity, and location
37.5-hour work week, permanent full-time position
Opportunities for professional growth and advancement

Qualifications

Graduate degree in biology, toxicology, chemistry, soil science, geoscience, or related scientific field.
This position is suited for an intermediate environmental risk assessor who is comfortable leading technical components of projects while continuing to expand their expertise in risk assessment and regulatory frameworks.
5 to 10+ years of experience in preparing high-quality human health and/or ecological risk assessments for a variety of audiences including clients and other stakeholders, Indigenous communities, and regulators.
Hands-on experience in environmental data collection and evaluation, including the design and implementation of community surveys.
Strong analytical skills, with demonstrated proficiency in data management, spreadsheet development, and automation.
Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal, with the ability to collaborate effectively in multidisciplinary teams, prepare clear technical reports, and develop engaging presentation materials.
Experience with scope development, budgeting, and proposal preparation.
Working knowledge of biological and toxicological studies (e.g., benthic community assessments, toxicity tests etc.), an asset.
Experience with risk assessments under O.Reg. 153/04, an asset.
Experience with soil vapour and indoor air quality assessments at contaminated sites, an asset.,
Valid driver’s license and willingness to occasionally travel to sites/clients
Membership or eligibility for membership in a professional organization (e.g., R.P.Bio., P.Geo., P.Eng., P.Ag., P.Chem., or QPRA).

The Opportunity

Tetra Tech is looking for a full-time Risk Assessor based out of our Cincinnati, OH office. Remote workers outside of the area are also encouraged to apply.

Position Summary

Tetra Tech, a leading environmental and engineering consulting firm, is seeking a Risk Assessor who can prepare and review human health and ecological risk assessments and assist in developing remedial strategies for brownfields and other sites where hazardous substances or petroleum pose a potential or known environmental or regulatory concern. Specific experience in preparing risk assessments following technical guidance under the Ohio EPA Voluntary Action Program (VAP) is preferred.

The position is based out of our Cincinnati, Ohio office and would involve providing support on various environmental projects (primarily under Ohio EPA VAP and US EPA) throughout the Midwest, predominantly within Ohio. This position will support a variety of contracts, including federal, state, and commercial clients. The ideal candidate will have excellent technical writing and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work successfully both independently and in team settings.

Essential Job Functions

The following duties are considered essential to the role. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these essential functions:

This position will support environmental investigations within an office setting predominantly, with the following general responsibilities:

Support field surveys and assessments through data collection and evaluation of environmental conditions.
Analyze large environmental datasets.
Conduct statistical and spatial data analyses, and prepare tables, figures, and other exhibits.
Perform contaminant fate/transport and exposure modeling.
Review and interpret environmental and toxicological studies and reports.
Conduct human and ecological risk assessments in accordance with federal and state guidance, with emphasis on Ohio EPA VAP.
Prepare written documents such as letters, memoranda, proposals, work plans, and investigative reports.
Support remedial strategy development for contaminated sites.

Why Tetra Tech

At Tetra Tech, we are Leading with Science to solve the world’s most complex challenges. Our industry-leading experts in engineering and consulting are committed to driving positive change in communities around the world. For over 60 years, we have been at the forefront of innovation and sustainability. Today we stand as a market leader, offering cutting-edge solutions in water, environment, energy, and international development. Our work has improved more than 625 million lives around the world.

Your Impact

Join Tetra Tech to make a real difference. Our work leverages cutting-edge technologies, advanced analytics, and the expertise of world-class scientists and engineers to create meaningful change around the world. Discover your full potential – join us to advance your career while leaving a lasting legacy.

Required Qualifications

5 to 10+ years of environmental consulting or related experience.
Bachelor’s degree in Biology, Ecology, Environmental Science, or a related field with a background in risk assessment is required.
Previous experience with completion of human health and/or ecological risk assessments under state or federal environmental programs.
Must possess strong analytical, organizational, and communication skills (both written and verbal).
Must be highly motivated, customer focused, and work well in a team environment.

This position requires driving on a regular basis. Passing a motor vehicle record background check and maintaining a valid driver's license and good driving record is required.

Preferred Qualifications

Previous experience with completion of human health and/or ecological risk assessments under Ohio EPA VAP.
Experience and knowledge of U.S. EPA, Ohio EPA VAP, and/or Ohio BUSTR.
Field data collection experience, including soil, groundwater, soil gas, surface water, and/or sediment sampling.
OSHA 40-Hour HAZWOPER with 8-Hour Refresher.

Physical Requirements

Must be able to walk around project sites in all types of terrain and be physically able to carry up to 50 pounds of equipment.
Must be able to complete annual medical monitoring program.

Work Environment / Environmental Factors

This position will require outdoor work within the U.S. during all seasons, including peak summer and winter conditions.
Overnight travel may also be required that could be in excess of 10%.

Additional Information

40 hour/week Monday through Friday schedule. Occasional overtime may be required as needed on project and field events.
Field work/travel encompass up to 20% of the position.
Position is open to remote work.

Life at Tetra Tech

The Perks Of Working At Tetra Tech Include

Comprehensive and market-competitive benefits.
Merit-based financial rewards.
Flexibility and company-wide commitment to work/life balance.
Collaborative team atmosphere that values the contributions of all employees.
Learning and development opportunities for ongoing professional growth.

Tetra Tech offers comprehensive benefit options that allow employees to design a plan based on individual needs and assists in planning for long-term financial security. Available benefits include medical, dental and vision insurance, term life, disability, accidental death & dismemberment coverage, Flexible Spending Account (FSA), Health Spending Account (HSA), time off with pay, 401k retirement plan, and an Employee Stock Purchase Plan.

jobs.title: Environmental Toxicologist (Biochemist)
jobs.description:
Battelle delivers when others can’t. We conduct research and development, manage national laboratories, design and manufacture products and deliver critical services for our clients—whether they are a multi-national corporation, a small start-up or a government agency.

We recognize and appreciate the value and contributions of individuals from a wide range of backgrounds and experiences and welcome all qualified individuals to apply.

Job Summary

Battelle’s Life Science Research Center (LSR) in West Jefferson, OH comprises world-class toxicology facilities and expert staff who support critical toxicology, safety pharmacology, and inhalation research programs for our pharmaceutical, biotechnology, agrichemical, industrial, and government clients. Our multidisciplinary, integrated approach to problem-solving accelerates innovation while maintaining the highest standards of quality and compliance.

We are currently seeking a Environmental Toxicologist (Biochemist IV) to provide technical leadership and discipline oversight within our Environmental Hazard programs. This position functions as a subject matter expert and Discipline Lead for toxicology, focusing on strategy implementation and day-to-day execution of complex toxicology studies in a regulated research environment. The Environmental Toxicologist ensures the scientific quality, compliance, and timely completion of non-clinical toxicology studies, including oversight of study design, conduct, data analysis, and reporting. In close collaboration with Project Management and cross-functional teams (Chemistry, Inhalation, Pathology, Quality Assurance, etc.), this individual will orchestrate predictable study execution and seamless integration across disciplines to achieve client and program objectives. By providing day-to-day technical guidance and operational rigor, the Environmental Toxicologist plays a key role in supporting the program’s principal investigator (PI) and Program Manager (PM) – ensuring the scientific and delivery excellence that allows program leadership to focus on high-level strategy and client engagement.

Responsibilities

Provide expert toxicology leadership on multiple concurrent studies, serving as Study Director or Discipline Lead for in vivo environmental toxicology and related studies (e.g., inhalation, biodistribution, pharmacokinetic, efficacy studies) for government and commercial sponsors.
Review and oversee all scientific elements of toxicology projects, including study protocols, amendments, data, and reports, to ensure scientific integrity, GLP compliance, and alignment with sponsor requirements. Guarantee that deliverables undergo thorough internal technical review and quality control prior to final approval by PIs or external release, upholding Battelle’s reputation for excellence.
Drive on-schedule execution of toxicology studies by closely integrating toxicology plans with program/project timelines, monitoring key milestones (study set-up, dosing, data analysis, reporting) and proactively identifying/mitigating risks (e.g., resource constraints, data variability) to prevent delays. Quickly escalate critical risks or issues with recommended solutions to PMs/PIs to maintain a “no surprises” environment for clients and stakeholders.
Coordinate cross-functional activities across disciplines (Toxicology, Chemistry, Inhalation, Pathology, etc.) and interface with other Discipline Leads, ensuring consistent methodologies and smooth handoffs. Lead or participate in interdisciplinary planning and problem-solving sessions to align study execution with the broader program and operational goals.
Mentor and develop toxicology staff (Study Directors, scientists, technicians), providing scientific guidance and frameworks for execution. Establish knowledge-sharing forums and best practice reviews to continuously improve team proficiency, build capacity (reducing single points of failure), and promote a culture of excellence and collaboration.
Maintain disciplined communication and meeting cadences. Lead regular toxicology team meetings and contribute to program status updates, ensuring key decisions, changes, and progress are clearly communicated across the team and to leadership. Uphold meeting best practices (agendas, action tracking) to create a transparent, efficient operating environment.
Champion process improvements in toxicology operations and study workflows. Identify and implement efficiency and quality enhancements (e.g., streamlined review cycles, improved scheduling processes) and contribute to the program’s operational playbook, driving continuous improvement and scalability in how toxicology studies are executed.
Contribute to program growth and success. May lead or collaborate with business development and project management teams in proposal development, scope definition, and client discussions as needed. Support leadership in meeting program objectives and financial targets by ensuring successful, on-time completion of toxicology studies within budget constraints, including adherence to contract specifications and proactive management of resources.
Advance scientific innovation and external visibility. Identify opportunities to contribute to invention disclosures, intellectual property development, and novel methodological approaches that enhance program impact. Actively contribute to scientific publications, technical presentations, and participation in professional conferences or peer review activities, strengthening Battelle’s reputation and visibility within the toxicology and broader scientific community.

Key Qualifications

Education & Experience: Ph.D. in Toxicology or a related life science field with at least 5 years of experience in toxicology research; OR M.S. with 8+ years of prior relevant experience; OR B.S. with 10+ years of prior experience. Educational background or research focus in biochemistry, pharmacology, environmental toxicology, or related science is strongly preferred.
Technical Expertise: Demonstrated expertise in the design, execution, and interpretation of in vivo toxicology studies (e.g., environmental toxicity, inhalation toxicology, chemical safety) with a track record of scientific publications or study reports documenting impactful results. Proficiency in applying GLP principles and regulatory guidelines (e.g., OECD, ICH for nonclinical studies) to ensure compliance in study conduct and data management.
Project Execution & Team Leadership: Strong project management and organizational skills; able to manage multiple studies concurrently, meet deadlines consistently, and coordinate cross-functional teams in a matrix environment. Experience leading or guiding technical staff with an emphasis on quality control, problem-solving, and risk management in study execution.
Communication & Collaboration: Exceptional verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to convey complex toxicology concepts to diverse audiences (technical and non-technical) clearly and effectively. Proactive communicator adept at fostering collaboration across disciplines and keeping stakeholders informed to ensure alignment.
Additional Requirements: Must be willing to participate in random drug screening. Legal authorization to work in the U.S. is required (Battelle does not provide sponsorship for employment-based visas for this position). Must be capable of meeting applicable security and safety requirements for work in specialized laboratory environments (such as biosafety procedures for GLP studies).

Preferred Qualifications

Professional Certification: Diplomate of the American Board of Toxicology (DABT) certification (or eligibility/preparedness to attain certification within 1 year).
Advanced Expertise: Additional postdoctoral experience or publications in environmental toxicology, inhalation toxicology, or related fields.
Project/Program Experience: Prior experience serving as a Study Director or Discipline Lead on GLP-compliant toxicology studies, especially for government research (e.g., NIH/NIEHS, DoD).

Benefits: Live an Extraordinary Life

We care about your well-being, not just on the job. Battelle offers comprehensive and competitive benefits to help you live your best life.

Balance life through a compressed work schedule: Most of our team follows a flexible, compressed work schedule that allows for every other Friday off—giving you a dedicated day to accomplish things in your personal life without using vacation time.
Enjoy enhanced work flexibility, including a hybrid arrangement: You have options for where and when you work. Our Together with Flexibility model allows you to work 60% in-office and 40% remote, with Monday and Tuesday as common in-office days, dependent on team and position needs.
Take time to recharge: You get paid time off to support work-life balance and keep motivated.
Prioritize wellness: Stay healthy with medical, dental, and vision coverage with wellness incentives and benefits plus a variety of optional supplemental benefits.
Better together: Coverage for partners, gender-affirming care and health support, and family formation support.
Build your financial future: Build financial stability with an industry-leading 401(k) retirement savings plan. For most employees, we put in 5 percent whether you contribute or not, and match your contributions on top of that.
Advance your education: Tuition assistance is available to pursue higher education.

A Work Environment Where You Succeed

For brilliant minds in science, technology, engineering and business operations, Battelle is the place to do the greatest good by solving humanity’s most pressing challenges and creating a safer, healthier and more secure world.

You will have the opportunity to thrive in a culture that inspires you to:

Apply your talent to challenging and meaningful projects
Receive select funding to pursue ideas in scientific and technological discovery
Partner with world-class experts in a collaborative environment
Nurture and develop the next generation of scientific leaders
Give back to and improve our communities

Vaccinations & Safety Protocols

Battelle may require employees, based on job duties, work location, and/or its clients’ requirements to follow certain safety protocols and to be vaccinated against a variety of viruses, bacteria, and diseases as a condition of employment and continued employment and to provide documentation that they are fully vaccinated. If applicable, Battelle will provide reasonable accommodations based on a qualified disability or medical condition through the Americans with Disabilities Act or the Rehabilitation Act or for a sincerely held religious belief under Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 (and related state laws).

Battelle is an equal opportunity employer. We provide employment and opportunities for advancement, compensation, training, and growth according to individual merit, without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy), national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital status, age, genetic information, disability, veteran-status veteran or military status, or any other characteristic protected under applicable Federal, state, or local law. Our goal is for each staff member to have the opportunity to grow to the limits of their abilities and to achieve personal and organizational objectives. We will support positive programs for equal treatment of all staff and full utilization of all qualified employees at all levels within Battelle.

Environmental compliance-oriented

jobs.title: Environmental Specialist
jobs.description:
About This Role

We are currently seeking an experienced Environment Specialist to join the Asset Retirement HSE team of a leading global oil & gas organisation.

This is a 2-year contract opportunity working on a FIFO 2 weeks on / 2 weeks off roster, providing hands-on environmental support across a major Asset Retirement program encompassing decommissioning, remediation, well abandonment and associated project activities.

Reporting to the HSE Team Lead - Asset Retirement, you will work closely with project teams, contractors, operational personnel and environmental specialists to support the safe, compliant and environmentally responsible delivery of Asset Retirement activities.

The Role

The Environment Specialist will provide practical environmental guidance and assurance across field-based operations and projects, with a strong focus on environmental compliance, risk management and continuous improvement.

Key responsibilities will include:

Conducting field-based environmental assurance, verification and validation activities across Asset Retirement worksites.
Supporting environmental monitoring and sampling programs covering air, water, waste and soil.
Providing support across waste management, fauna handling and other environmental field activities.
Supporting environmental risk assessments and the implementation of appropriate controls.
Developing and delivering environmental training, awareness initiatives and environmental leadership programs.
Supporting teams and contractors to build environmental capability and improve environmental performance.
Participating in projects and working groups relating to environmental risk, waste management, contaminated land, rehabilitation and continuous improvement.
Building effective working relationships across HSE, project teams, contractors, business partners, regulators and corporate environmental teams.
Supporting environmental regulatory approvals, compliance obligations, audits and reporting requirements.
Participating in Incident Management and Emergency Response activities, including emergency exercises and response events.
Supporting environmental and wildlife response activities where required.
Facilitating incident investigations and learning events using recognised methodologies including 5-Why, SAFE, Why-Tree and Learning Teams.
Applying Human and Organizational Performance (HOP) principles to support sustainable improvements in environmental and HSE performance.

Requirements

To be considered for this opportunity, you will ideally have:

A Diploma or Degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Management or a related discipline.
Demonstrated experience applying environmental management systems and environmental risk management principles in a practical operational or project environment.
Strong field-based environmental experience and the ability to provide practical advice to frontline personnel and contractors.
Excellent stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to influence without direct authority.
The confidence to operate as a visible HSE professional and engage effectively with leaders, frontline workers, contractors and regulators.
Strong communication skills with the ability to adapt your approach to different stakeholder groups.
The ability and willingness to work a FIFO 2:2 roster.
You must have current right to work in Australia to be considered for this role

Experience in some or all of the following will be highly regarded:

Environmental assurance, compliance,monitoring and sampling
Contaminated land management and remediation.
Waste management.
Fauna handling.
Emergency response and oil spill response..
Major projects, construction or operational environments.
Decommissioning, remediation or Asset Retirement activities.

Benefits

Work for a global oil and gas business
FIFO 2:2 roster
2 year contract
Salary sacrificing
Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
Corporate discounts

**Overview**  
We are seeking a highly motivated Cleanroom Environmental Monitoring Technicians to join our team in PAL's Microbiology \& EM services for Biotech, Pharma, medical device, and Compounding Pharmacies companies. The positions are temporary with potential for becoming regular employee later on. This role is essential in ensuring compliance with regulatory standards and maintaining the integrity of our laboratory processes. Services include validation of clean rooms, water systems and compressed gases systems, and routine sampling of these systems. EM techs must follow proper safety practices and comply with GMP requirements as needed and with client requirements. We are looking for a person willing to work hard, able to work overtime, start work early and sometimes weekends.

**Responsibilities**

* Perform in\-house and field environmental monitoring sampling at client facilities (cleanrooms, water systems and compressed gases systems).
* Perform water testing such as bioburden, TOC, endotoxin and conductivity.

Requirements

* Minimum AS degree in science with a concentration in microbiology. The position requires at least 1 year of hands\-on experience in microbiology or EM testing in an FDA GMP regulated.
* Hands on experience in endotoxin testing, cleanroom Environmental monitoring, water testing and USP microbial methods.
* Experience performing USP, FDA BAM, AOAC, and ISO microbiology test procedures for biotech, pharmaceutical, and other FDA regulated products.
* Excellent organizational skills along with good written and verbal communication skills in English.
* Ability to follow instructions and work as a team member.
* Valid driver’s license required.
* Ability to start early (6am), work overtime and weekends as needed to complete projects.
* Ability to work in a fast\-paced environment.
* Ability to gown into a coverall and work in a cleanroom environment for long hours.
* Ability to stand and be on your feet for long hours.
* Understands, reads and comprehends English fluently.
* Ability to lift and move 20 pounds.
* Legal to work in the USA.
* Must pass background check and drug testing.

Pay: $25\.20 \- $30\.35 per hour

At WSP, you can access our global scale, contribute to landmark projects and connect with the brightest minds in your field to do the best work of your life. You can embrace your curiosity in a culture that celebrates new ideas and diverse perspectives. You can experience a world of opportunity and the chance to shape a career as unique as you


We're looking for an **Environmental Scientist** to join our **Contaminated Land Management (CLM) team** in Sydney. This is an exciting opportunity to work on diverse contaminated land and groundwater projects across New South Wales and nationally, helping clients understand, manage and remediate environmental risks. The role is suited to an environmental professional with **at least 2 years' commercial experience** who is looking to build technical expertise, strengthen project delivery skills and take the next step in their consulting career.


As part of our established multidisciplinary Environment business, you'll collaborate with experienced contaminated land specialists, geologists, hydrogeologists and environmental engineers to deliver innovative solutions for site investigation, environmental due diligence, risk assessment and remediation projects. Our work spans mining, petroleum\-contaminated land, industrial facilities and government assets, supporting the rehabilitation and redevelopment of complex sites.


This role offers a balance of fieldwork, technical reporting, project coordination and client engagement, providing exposure to a broad range of challenging and rewarding contaminated land projects.


**About the Role**

As an **Environmental Scientist** , you'll play a key role in delivering contaminated land investigations and remediation projects while developing your technical and project management capabilities. You'll work closely with experienced consultants and project managers, contributing to high\-quality client outcomes across a variety of sectors.


**Your responsibilities will include:**

* Conducting contaminated land and groundwater investigations, including soil, groundwater and vapour sampling programs.
* Coordinating fieldwork activities, contractors and subcontractors to ensure safe, compliant and high\-quality project delivery.
* Interpreting environmental data and developing conceptual site models.
* Preparing technical reports, environmental assessments and remediation documentation.
* Assisting with project coordination, including budgets, schedules, scope and stakeholder communication.
* Applying environmental legislation, standards and contaminated land guidelines to project delivery.
* Contributing to proposal preparation and supporting business development opportunities.
Mentoring graduates and supporting a strong culture of safety, quality and technical excellence.  
* 

**About You**

We're seeking an environmental professional who combines strong technical skills with a passion for contaminated land management and delivering exceptional client outcomes.


You will bring:


* Bachelor's degree in Earth Sciences, Environmental Engineering or equivalent.
* **At least 2\+ years’ experience** in contaminated land assessment, remediation or environmental consulting.
* Experience undertaking contaminated land and groundwater investigations and field programs.
* Understanding of contaminated land legislation, standards and regulatory frameworks.
* Strong data interpretation and technical report writing skills.
* Ability to coordinate multiple project tasks while maintaining quality, safety and budget requirements.
* Experience supervising contractors, subcontractors or junior team members.
* Excellent communication skills and a collaborative approach to working with clients and colleagues.
Commitment to safety, innovation, quality and technical excellence.  
* 

**Why WSP?**

At WSP, we value our people and our reputation. We are locally dedicated with international scale, future\-focused, collaborative and empowering — and we’re looking for people who share those values.


You’ll be part of a team that delivers technical excellence while keeping client outcomes, sustainability, quality and safety at the centre of what we do. You’ll also have the opportunity to grow your leadership capability, contribute to meaningful projects and help shape better outcomes for communities and clients.


Imagine a better future for you and a better future for us all.


Join our close\-knit community of talented individuals who share your passion for making a positive impact.


**With us, you can. Apply today.**

jobs.description:
**What if you could do the kind of work the world needs?**

At WSP, you can access our global scale, contribute to landmark projects and connect with the brightest minds in your field to do the best work of your life. You can embrace your curiosity in a culture that celebrates new ideas and diverse perspectives. You can experience a world of opportunity and the chance to shape a career as unique as you


We're looking for an **Associate Environmental Scientist** to join **our Contaminated Land Management (CLM) team** in Sydney. In this influential role, you'll provide technical leadership across a diverse portfolio of contaminated land projects while mentoring emerging professionals and helping shape the growth of our CLM business across New South Wales and nationally.


Working alongside talented specialists across WSP's multidisciplinary Environmental business, you'll deliver future\-ready solutions for site investigation, environmental due diligence, portfolio assessment, advisory services and remediation planning. Our projects span mining, petroleum\-contaminated land, industrial facilities and government assets, helping clients rehabilitate, repurpose and unlock the value of complex sites.


This is an opportunity to combine technical excellence, project leadership, client engagement and people development within one of Australia's leading environmental consulting teams.


**About the Role**

As an **Associate Environmental Scientist** , you'll lead the delivery of contaminated land projects from investigation through to remediation, providing trusted technical advice while supporting the continued growth of our people and clients. You'll play a key role in delivering successful project outcomes, developing long\-term client relationships and fostering technical excellence across the team.


**Your responsibilities will include:**

* Leading contaminated land investigations, including soil, groundwater and vapour assessments.
* Providing technical leadership, review and advice across complex contaminated land and remediation projects.
* Managing project performance, including budgets, schedules, resources and risk.
* Developing and maintaining strong client relationships while acting as a trusted advisor.
* Preparing and reviewing technical reports and recommendations in accordance with relevant legislation, standards and guidelines.
* Leading and supporting remediation planning and implementation activities.
* Mentoring and developing junior team members while promoting a strong safety and quality culture.
Supporting business development activities, including proposals, pursuits and identifying opportunities to grow client relationships.  
* 

**About You**

We're seeking a respected contaminated land professional with strong technical capability, leadership experience and a passion for developing people and delivering exceptional client outcomes.


**You will bring:**

* Bachelor's degree in Earth Sciences, Environmental Engineering or equivalent.
* At least 7 years' experience in contaminated land assessment, remediation and environmental consulting.
* Strong understanding of NSW contaminated land legislation, frameworks and regulatory processes.
* Proven experience managing project risk, budgets, schedules and delivery on substantial projects.
* Demonstrated ability to prepare and review high\-quality technical reports and provide practical client\-focused advice.
* Experience developing and maintaining strong client relationships.
* Proven capability supervising, mentoring and developing environmental professionals and field teams.
* Strong communication skills with the ability to guide clients through regulatory processes and complex technical challenges.
Commitment to safety, quality and technical excellence.  
* 

**Why WSP?**

At WSP, we value our people and our reputation. We are locally dedicated with international scale, future\-focused, collaborative and empowering — and we’re looking for people who share those values.


You’ll be part of a team that delivers technical excellence while keeping client outcomes, sustainability, quality and safety at the centre of what we do. You’ll also have the opportunity to grow your leadership capability, contribute to meaningful projects and help shape better outcomes for communities and clients.


Imagine a better future for you and a better future for us all.


Join our close\-knit community of talented individuals who share your passion for making a positive impact.


**With us, you can. Apply today.**

At SLR our purpose is to Make Sustainability Happen. SLR is an international environmental consultancy with a globally recognised reputation for providing high quality tailored services. We have an opportunity for an experienced Contaminated Land Consultant to join our Perth office on a permanent full-time basis.

Full and unrestricted working rights in Australia.

jobs.title: Environmental Scientist/Project Manager
jobs.description:
Do you like working with different project teams in a fast\-paced environment? Are you interested in joining an organization focused on making a positive impact? If so, we'd like to talk with you about growing with us.


EnSafe is seeking a full\-time Environmental Scientist/Project Manager to join our team of professionals at our San Diego, CA, office.



This position has a requirement to work onsite, at the office, if needed relocation assistance may be offered to meet this expectation.


**What we are looking for**



An Environmental Scientist with proven experience managing environmental due diligence projects and a strong ability to translate complex findings into clear, defensible Phase I ESA reports. You'll work with clients across California and beyond, managing projects from site assessment through final reporting while gaining exposure to Phase II investigations, environmental sampling, and emerging areas such as PFAS risk evaluation.



Joining our team means immersing yourself in an environment that nurtures creativity, encourages collaboration at all levels, fosters a supportive culture, and facilitates professional development.


***Key responsibilities of this position include***


***What you will be doing:***


* Perform and manage Phase I Environmental Site Assessments in accordance with ASTM and applicable regulatory requirements.
* Conduct site reconnaissance, historical research, regulatory database review, interviews, and other due diligence activities.
* Prepare clear, technically sound Phase I ESA reports and recommendations.
* Manage multiple Phase I ESA projects, including scope, schedule, budget, subcontractors, client communication, and deliverables.
* Provide technical and peer review of Phase I ESA reports as experience permits.
* Support Phase II environmental site investigations and other due diligence activities when warranted.
* Plan and conduct environmental sampling activities involving soil, groundwater, soil vapor, indoor air, surface water, or other environmental media.
* Prepare work plans, technical memoranda, investigation reports, and proposals.
* Communicate findings and environmental risk considerations clearly to clients and project teams.
* Coordinate work with junior staff and provide technical guidance and mentoring.
* Support environmental compliance projects based on experience and workload, which may include hazardous materials and hazardous waste management, SPCC, stormwater, wastewater, EPCRA/Tier II, or related regulatory requirements.
* Participate in business development activities, including preparation of scopes, budgets, proposals, and support for existing client relationships.
* Travel periodically to project sites throughout California and as needed, elsewhere in the United States.


***Minimum Skills and Requirements***


* Bachelor's degree in environmental science, Geology, Environmental Engineering, or a related scientific or engineering discipline.
* Approximately 6 or more years of relevant environmental consulting experience.
* Demonstrated experience preparing Phase I Environmental Site Assessments.
* Strong technical writing and report preparation skills.
* Ability to independently conduct site reconnaissance and evaluate environmental conditions.
* Working knowledge of environmental due diligence practices and applicable federal and state environmental regulations.
* Ability to manage schedules, budgets, client expectations, and multiple concurrent assignments.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills.
* Strong critical\-thinking and problem\-solving skills.
* Ability and willingness to travel to support project work.
* Valid driver's license and ability to perform field activities associated with environmental site assessments.


***Preferred Qualifications***


***The following experience would be beneficial but is not required:***


* Experience managing Phase I ESA programs or providing technical/peer review.
* Qualification as an Environmental Professional under ASTM/AAI requirements.
* Phase II ESA, subsurface investigation, soil, groundwater, or vapor assessment experience.
* Environmental compliance experience, including hazardous waste, hazardous materials, SPCC, stormwater, wastewater, CERS/HMBP, or EPCRA/Tier II reporting.
* Experience supporting industrial, commercial real estate, logistics/warehouse, energy, municipal, or similar clients.
* Professional Geologist (PG), Professional Engineer (PE), or other relevant professional certification.
* Building sciences or hazardous building materials experience.
* Experience with asbestos\-containing materials, lead\-based paint, mold/microbial assessments, or related building surveys.
* California asbestos or lead certifications.
* 40\-hour HAZWOPER training.


**Why Join EnSafe?**


* **Employee\-Owned Advantage**  

EnSafe is 100% employee\-owned, with an ESOP (Employee Stock Ownership Plan) since 1997\. That means when EnSafe succeeds, you succeed too, turning company growth directly into shared rewards.
* **Commitment to Growth and Wellness**  

The company supports personalized career development, mentorship, and employee wellness initiatives such as health tracking tools.
* **Purpose‑Driven Work**  

EnSafe's mission focuses on impactful environmental, health, and safety consulting—making a real difference in communities and is backed by its long\-standing technical credibility.
* **Safety as a Value, Not Just a Service**  

Safety is deeply embedded in our culture, prioritizing employee well\-being in addition to helping clients maintain compliance. We stress that *"safety is part of everything we do."*
* **A Culture of Freedom \& Ownership**  

At EnSafe, our career philosophy is built on freedom. The freedom to take initiative, achieve your goals, and shape your own career path Employees are encouraged to pursue growth in a flexible, entrepreneurial environment.
* **Challenging, Creative Work**  

Workdays at EnSafe are anything but ordinary,

jobs.title: Senior Environmental Specialist
jobs.description:
About Tower Semiconductor

Looking for a career path in the high-tech industry? Become part of a team focused on delivering the most exciting semiconductor technology in the world! If you enjoy working with others in a dynamic, fast-paced environment and are looking for an opportunity to grow your career in this exciting industry, then Tower Semiconductor is the place to be!

Tower Semiconductor, the leading foundry of high-value analog semiconductor solutions, provides technology, development, and process platforms for analog integrated circuits to more than 300 customers worldwide across growing markets such as communications, mobile, infrastructure, consumer, industrial, automotive, medical, and aerospace and defense, among others.

Join Tower and become part of a dynamic organization with exceptionally talented and dedicated team members who work collaboratively to provide best-in-class technological solutions to our clients.

Job Description

An Environmental Specialist is responsible for ensuring uninterrupted manufacturing operations through proactive environmental compliance, risk identification, regulatory engagement, and timely execution of critical Environmental programs. The role supports semiconductor manufacturing operations by ensuring compliance with environmental regulations governing air emissions, wastewater treatment, hazardous waste management, and chemical handling.

This position works closely with manufacturing, facilities, engineering, operations, and corporate EHS teams to minimize environmental risk, maintain regulatory compliance, and support safe and reliable fab operations.

This Job Is For You If

You can ensure compliance with federal, state, and local environmental regulations (e.g., 40 CFR, 30 TAC) related to air emissions, hazardous waste, wastewater, stormwater, and chemical management.
You can proactively identify compliance risks, operational vulnerabilities, and permitting gaps, and escalate issues early to management with clear mitigation plans.
You can maintain accurate environmental records, emissions inventories, permit tracking systems, and regulatory submissions to ensure timely and compliant reporting
You can oversee hazardous waste management, hazardous material shipping, and Spill Prevention Control and Countermeasure (SPCC) programs.
You can manage air compliance programs including stack testing, Leak Detection and Repair (LDAR), greenhouse gas (GHG) monitoring, and criteria pollutant tracking.
You can monitor wastewater treatment systems and implement Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plans (SWPPP).
You can lead regulatory inspections and agency interactions with professionalism, technical competence, and strong preparation.
You can conduct facility audits and inspections of chemical storage, waste accumulation, and environmental control systems.
You can investigate environmental incidents, determine root causes, and drive timely corrective and preventive actions (CAPAs).
You can coordinate effectively across operations, facilities, engineering, production, and corporate EHS teams to ensure alignment and execution of environmental priorities.
You can develop and maintain environmental procedures, standards, and training programs to ensure ongoing compliance and operational readiness.
You can prepare and submit environmental reports including Toxic Release Inventory (TRI), Tier II, emissions inventories, and Discharge Monitoring Reports.
You can implement programs that minimize environmental risk, business interruption, and operational impact.
You can manage multiple competing priorities in a fast-paced manufacturing environment while maintaining high accuracy, responsiveness, and attention to detail.

Job Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Occupational Safety and Health, or a related field required.
Minimum 5 years of environmental compliance experience, preferably within semiconductor manufacturing or other highly regulated industrial operations.
Extensive knowledge of environmental regulations, permitting requirements, and regulatory reporting.
Experience managing environmental compliance programs related to air, waste, water, and hazardous materials.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Strong organizational, analytical, and project management skills.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and environmental tracking/reporting systems.
Ability to conduct inspections in manufacturing and industrial environments.
Must be able to lift and carry up to 25 pounds as needed.
Ability to sit, stand, walk, and work on a computer for extended periods as required by the role.

Preferred Characteristics

Strong sense of ownership and accountability
Proactive communicator with excellent follow-through
Ability to work independently with minimal supervision
Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities
Comfortable operating in high-visibility, high-responsibility environments
Strong cross-functional collaboration and coordination skills
High attention to detail and strong organizational discipline

Compensation: $106,000/year - $124,000/year

jobs.description:
Company Overview

EKI Environment & Water, Inc. (EKI) is an employee-owned environmental, water resources, and engineering consulting firm serving private- and public-sector clients throughout the United States. If you are interested in improving the environment and advancing your career, then EKI is the place for you.

The PFAS Program Manager reports to the Executive Vice President, ESG, and is responsible for coordinating and advancing EKI’s national PFAS practice. Working collaboratively with EKI’s PFAS technical experts, Regional Directors, Technical Directors, Principals, and Project Managers, the PFAS Program Manager will organize and integrate EKI’s PFAS capabilities, support high-quality project execution, identify and develop opportunities with existing and new client relationships, develop innovative service offerings, and help position EKI as a recognized leader in PFAS consulting.

The PFAS Program Manager will serve as a catalyst for collaboration across EKI’s PFAS practitioners and will help connect technical capabilities with client and market needs. The role combines technical project execution, practice development, internal coordination, client engagement, and business development. Success in the position will require strong technical judgement, the ability to work effectively with and leverage EKI’s subject-matter experts, and the leadership and initiative to build a coordinated and effective PFAS practice.

Principal Duties & Responsibilities

Your responsibilities may include, but will not be limited to the following:

Advance EKI's PFAS practice by bringing together PFAS practitioners across the company; fostering and promoting knowledge sharing; developing training programs; supporting recruitment of PFAS professionals; identifying technical capabilities, resource needs, and capability gaps; and helping establish priorities and initiatives for continued development of the practice.
Develop and expand PFAS opportunities with strategic clients by working with Regional Directors, Technical Directors, Practice Area Directors, Principals, Project Managers, and technical staff to identify PFAS needs and opportunities; developing client-specific strategies; and connecting EKI’s PFAS capabilities with client needs.

Title: EHS Specialist

Locations: Mountain View, CA (Fully Onsite)

Duration: Contract (6+ Months - Extendable)

Client: Aviation & Aerospace domain

Job Description:

We are seeking EHS Specialists (Contractors) to join our team. The goal of this position is to support the hands-on deployment, execution, and monitoring of practical EHS programs, ensuring our day-to-day workplace operations actively embody our core cultural behavior: “Safety Is Our Cornerstone.” You will join the EHS team, working boots on the ground to maintain total regulatory compliance and evaluate hazard points across our fast-paced aerospace environments.
Due to the nature of the work required for this position, this is an onsite opportunity. You will be required to work from our Mountain View, CA office, with flexibility to support or travel to local remote facilities as required by operational needs.
In this role you will own the day-to-day practical execution of core environmental, health, and safety protocols across R&D, Engineering, laboratories, and advanced manufacturing spaces.
As a mid-level specialist, you will bridge the gap between high-level policy and real-world implementation by conducting routine field audits, managing chemical and hazardous waste inventories, and facilitating employee safety training. You will collaborate directly with engineers, technicians, and floor operators to perform Job Hazard Analyses (JHAs) and incident investigations and ensure proper risk mitigation is in place. You will be instrumental in fostering a transparent, "Just Culture" workspace that enables cutting-edge aerospace development to proceed safely.

What you will do:

You will provide critical boots on the ground EHS support for our Bay Area facilities, helping to deploy specialized EHS solutions tailored to advanced air taxi development.
You will manage and maintain daily ownership over core workplace safety programs including Injury and Illness Prevention Plans (IIPP), Hazard Communication, Lockout/Tagout (LOTO), Machine Guarding, Respiratory Protection, Electrical Safety/NFPA 70e, and Powered Industrial Trucks.
You will support Engineering, Manufacturing, R&D, and Flight Test teams by conducting proactive Job Hazard Analyses (JHAs).
Executing field industrial hygiene assessments/sampling, including coordination with qualified third-party consultants.
You will help solve complex floor-level problems surrounding hazardous material classifications, maintaining updated Safety Data Sheet (SDS) documentation, and updating Hazardous Materials Business Plans (HMBP) via CERS.
You will routinely audit facilities, equipment, and work processes to identify structural risks, draft detailed inspection reports tracking corrective actions, and ensure timely closure of audit findings.
You will prepare, schedule, and lead instructor-led EHS training sessions, while actively participating in the internal Safety Collective .
You will lead responses to emergency situations onsite, such as fires (including from li-ion thermal runaway), electrical safety incidents, and other potential emergencies.

Requirements:

B.S. or B.A. in Environmental Safety, Occupational Safety and Health, Industrial Hygiene, or a related field with 5+ years of dedicated experience performing EHS duties in an industrial, hardware R&D, or manufacturing environment.
You have solid, applied knowledge of Cal-OSHA, federal OSHA standards, EPA requirements, and localized environmental regulatory baselines.
DOT / CA title 22 (Div. 4.5) for hazwaste management/signing manifests or ability to gain certification.
You have practical experience conducting accident/incident root-cause investigations, implementing corrective actions, and writing up standard compliance documentation.
You are certified or have the documented willingness to complete immediate DOT training to properly sign hazardous and universal waste manifests.
You are highly proficient with modern inspection technologies, workplace data tracking equipment, and standard office software applications.
You have strong interpersonal skills to influence internal customers.
Physically able to walk manufacturing and laboratory floors daily, conduct rigorous facility audits, and comfortably handle or carry related inspection and safety equipment.
Available to occasionally work flexible hours outside the standard workweek (including early mornings, evenings, or weekends) to support specialized systems test, flight test and manufacturing tasks or active incident investigations.
Experience in manufacturing or R&D environments preferred.

jobs.description:
Job Description

Position Description

We are seeking an experienced air quality professional to provide technical leadership and project delivery support within Ramboll’s Air and Climate Service Line. This position will focus on complex air dispersion modelling, air quality impact assessment, client advisory services, project management, and mentoring of junior to mid-level colleagues.

The role offers an opportunity to contribute to a growing national air quality practice while working collaboratively across Australian and global teams. Candidates with experience in digital tools, data workflows, automation, GIS, or cross-region technical coordination will be well placed to support ongoing innovation in how air quality services are delivered.

Air Quality Managing Consultant

Working within the Air and Climate Service Line you will be responsible for identifying, conducting and developing air quality projects based on an understanding of business needs, challenges, opportunities and the marketplace. Ramboll is seeking an experienced Air Quality Modelling professional for this position. Our ideal candidate is a technical leader with a proven track record of managing complex, multi-faceted air quality modelling projects, mentoring junior staff, and serving as a trusted advisor to clients. You would be responsible for overseeing project staff and be responsible for project delivery across the air quality team.

Your key responsibilities will be:

Technical Leadership: Lead and deliver complex air quality dispersion modelling and environmental impact assessment projects using regulatory and specialist models such as AERMOD, CALPUFF, CALMET, GRAL/GRAMM, TAPM and WRF. Develop innovative approaches to solving complex air quality, odour, emissions inventory and post-processing challenges.
Project Management: Manage air quality projects, including scope, schedule, budget, resources and quality, to support on-time and on-budget delivery that meets client expectations. Supervise project teams and delegate tasks to junior staff as required.
Technical Review and Quality Assurance: Provide senior-level QA/QC review and technical oversight of modelling analyses, emissions inventories, impact assessments, management plans, approval inputs and technical reports prepared by project teams.
Client and Regulatory Engagement: Act as a trusted client advisor through the full project lifecycle, from early strategy and scoping through approvals, compliance and implementation. Lead or support technical discussions with regulators and approval authorities on behalf of clients.
Staff Mentoring and Development: Mentor junior to mid-level air quality staff by providing technical guidance, training, review and career development support.
Business Development: Contribute technical and business content to proposals, develop scopes of work, support strategic client engagement and identify opportunities for growth in air quality services.
Digital and Cross-Region Collaboration: Support efficient project delivery through digital and technical innovation coordinating with Australian, APAC and global colleagues where specialist input or shared capability is required.

You will be part of the Australian Air and Climate Service Line working within the Air Quality Team as a Managing Consultant. You will lead the delivery of air quality projects, providing technical leadership, project management, and mentoring to junior team members, while supporting the ongoing growth and development of Ramboll’s national air quality capability.

Reporting to the National Air and Climate Practice Lead, you will play a key role in strengthening Ramboll’s air quality services and contributing to the continued success of the team. The position offers the opportunity to collaborate with colleagues across Australia, APAC and our global network to enhance project delivery, provide specialist technical expertise, drive digital innovation and promote technical excellence across Ramboll’s national air quality team.

Qualifications

About You

From the moment you start we will support your personal and professional development so that you can continue to grow with the company. While we look forward to supporting your continued learning and development, for this role we have identified some qualifications, skills and capabilities that will set you up for success:

Bachelor or Post Graduate degree in Environmental Science, Chemistry, Environmental Engineering, Chemical Engineering or related field with minimum 10 years of experience in air dispersion modelling and impact assessment.
Certified Air Quality Professional (CAQP) with the Clean Air Society of Australia and New Zealand and demonstrated involvement in profile raising activities (preferred).
Proficiency in meteorological and air dispersion modelling software such as AERMET, AERMOD, CALMET, CALPUFF, GRAMM, GRAL, TAPM and WRF.
Experience in development of air, odour and GHG emissions inventories across a wide range of industry sectors.
Strong technical knowledge and report writing skills, including preparation of Air Quality Impact Assessments, monitoring reports, Air Quality Management Plans and proposals.
Experienced project management skills, including direct client engagement. Business development skills are highly desirable, as is demonstrated experience in people management and/or mentoring.
Experience in ambient air quality monitoring, stack testing knowledge, climate risk assessment and/or noise monitoring and modelling, is not essential but would be highly regarded.
Experience in the following fields is highly desirable, including GIS software (e.g. ArcGIS Pro and Surfer), programming (e.g. R and Python), and analytical and data visualisation platforms (e.g. MS Power BI).
Excellent communication skills, including the ability to present complex technical, digital or data-related information clearly to clients, regulators and multidisciplinary project teams.

Additional Information

What we can offer you

Interesting and diverse projects
The opportunity to work with some of the best and brightest professionals in your field
Flexible work arrangements
Investment in your development
Leaders you can count on, guided by our Leadership Principles
Appreciation for the unique person you are
Inspiration from colleagues, clients, and projects.

We recognise that some candidates only apply when they tick every box. However, passion and potential often outweigh a perfect resume and Ramboll’s supportive learning culture can help you grow. So, if this role resonates with you but you don't meet all the requirements, we encourage you to apply. You might be the perfect fit for this opportunity or another within our team.

Work at the heart of sustainable change with Ramboll

Ramboll is a global architecture, engineering, and consultancy company. As a foundation-owned people company, founded in Denmark, we believe that the purpose of sustainable change is to create a thriving world for both nature and people. So, that’s where we start – and how we work. Our history is rooted in a clear vision of how a responsible company should act and being open and curious is a cornerstone of our culture. Ramboll employs more than 18,000 people globally across 35 countries. Ramboll experts deliver innovative solutions across Buildings, Transport, Water, Environment & Health, Energy, Management Consulting, and Architecture & Landscape. Combining local experience with global knowledge, we help shape the societies of tomorrow.

Equality, Diversity, and Inclusion

Equality, diversity, and inclusion are at the heart of what we do. At Ramboll, we believe that diversity is a strength and that different experiences and perspectives are essential to creating truly sustainable societies. We are committed to providing an inclusive and supportive work environment where everyone is able to flourish and reach their potential. We also know how important it is to achieve the right balance of where, when, and how much you work. At Ramboll, we offer flexibility as part of our positive and inclusive approach to work. We invite applications from candidates of all backgrounds and characteristics. jobs.title: Water Resources Project Manager
jobs.description:
Company Overview

EKI Environment & Water, Inc. (EKI) is an employee-owned, full service, engineering and environmental sciences consulting firm serving private- and public-sector clients throughout the United States. If you are interested in improving water management strategies and practices, improving the environment, and advancing your career, then EKI is the place for you.

The Water Resources Project Manager position reports to the Team Leader (TL) and is responsible for project management and technical oversight of high-impact projects with California clients from initial project planning through implementation. Projects include Sustainable Groundwater Management Act (SGMA) compliance and implementation, groundwater basin characterization, development of water budgets and water accounting frameworks, litigation support, water supply planning, and more.

Principal Duties & Responsibilities

Your responsibilities may include, but will not be limited to the following:

Coordinate SGMA implementation for groundwater basins across multiple Groundwater Sustainability Agencies
Oversee hydrogeologic conceptual model development, water balances, numerical models, and projects and/or management actions deemed necessary by the client
Prepare well-written technical memorandums or reports and studies, including groundwater sustainability plans (GSPs), SGMA annual reports, and periodic evaluations of adopted GSPs
Point of Contact for client; coordinate and lead client meetings and related meetings and coordination with external parties
Plan, organize, and manage staff to deliver quality project work products on time and within budget
Prepare effective presentations that efficiently communicate complex technical concepts to a broad audience
Manage project schedules, budgets, invoice preparation, and monthly progress reports
Provide quality assurance and quality control on and review of project deliverables
Support business development, including client development, preparing proposals, and presenting at conferences
Other duties as required

Qualifications & Requirements

Education

Bachelor’s degree in Hydrology, Geology, Earth Sciences, Engineering, or related field; Master’s or PhD degree preferred

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

Minimum of five (5) years of experience, with eight (8) or more years desirable for SGMA and related water resources projects
At least two (2) years of proven project management experience
Master's or PhD degree, and Professional Registration, or more than 12 years of demonstrated professional experience where Professional Registration is not available for degree, is desirable
Technical knowledge of SGMA, Groundwater Sustainability Plans, data management and visualization, ArcGIS, quantitative analysis (including numerical modeling), land subsidence, and technical writing
Knowledge of California groundwater and water planning regulations

Competencies

Must have excellent verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to communicate and coordinate effectively with clients, subconsultants, regulatory agencies, and members of the public as may be necessary to accomplish assigned objectives
Must have ability to multi-task, stay organized, work independently, and collaborate with various project teams
Must have demonstrated time management skills, strong work ethic, and attention to detail
Must have a strong desire to grow personally as well as professionally
Must have a great attitude and be eager to learn
Must have a current valid driver’s license

PHYSICAL DEMANDS & WORK ENVIRONMENT

Must be able to work in a fast-paced and dynamic environment
Must be able to lift up to 25 lbs
Must be able to work remaining in a stationary position, often standing or sitting for prolonged periods
Must be able to communicate with others to exchange information
Must be able to assess the accuracy, neatness and thoroughness of the work assigned

Travel Requirements

Must be able to travel occasionally, possibly overnight for customer meetings and site visits up to 25% of the time

SALARY RANGE

The expected base salary range for this position is $113,000 - $160,000 per year. Actual compensation will be determined based on a variety of factors, including the candidate's skills, experience, qualifications, and geographic location. In addition to base salary, this position is eligible for an annual performance bonus based on individual and company performance.

As an employee-owned firm, EKI offers a unique company culture with a corporate commitment to maintaining a positive work/life experience. EKI provides excellent compensation and comprehensive benefits packages, including career advancement opportunities, outstanding training opportunities, incentive compensation including bonuses, retirement benefits through an Employee Stock Ownership Program (ESOP) and 401(k) profit-sharing contributions, and group medical, vision, and dental benefits.

EKI Environment & Water, Inc. is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, pregnancy, genetic information, disability, status as a protected veteran, or any other protected category under applicable federal, state, and local laws.

NOTE: This job description is not intended to be all-inclusive and is not an exhaustive list of all required responsibilities, duties, and skills. This description may be amended at any time and employee may be assigned other related duties to meet the ongoing needs of the organization.

Notice To Third Party Agencies

EKI Environment & Water, Inc does not accept unsolicited resumes from recruiters or employment agencies. In the event a recruiter or agency submits a resume or candidate without a previously signed agreement and approved engagement request with EKI Environment & Water, Inc. reserves the right to pursue and hire those candidate(s) without any financial obligation to the recruiter or agency.
